### 205. A message's time, its copy and a send again

**Status: done.** Merged as `9934575` (PR #244; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** Each of the owner's messages has a foot once its turn has its answer
(`messages.js`): when it was sent, as short as its day allows ("14:05", "Yesterday, 14:05", "5 Oct, 14:05", the year too
when it was another; the full date where the pointer rests; `messageTime` in `dom.js`), a copy of it as it was written,
and **Send again**. A copy's icon turns to a check for a moment once the text is on the clipboard,
where a toast said it before. Send again sends the message once more with the files it came with, as the composer's
Enter does (into the queue or to the run while one works, otherwise as the chat's next run, whose page opens); the run
page sends both ways with one function (`deliver`), and what is typed in the composer stays. The files of an earlier
message are read from the first events of its run (its `attachments` event), those of a message that steered a run from
the message. The foot stands at the bubble's right edge, as quiet as the answer's; a turn at work keeps it back
(`.run-working` on the conversation while its run works, `.turn-working` on an earlier turn still going), and it shows
as the run ends, without a reload. The files a message came with stand between it and its foot. The answer's foot has an
icon to copy it, when it came and how it ended in sight; how long the run took still waits for the pointer (item 121). A
delegated run's page has no Send again: the run that delegated it wrote its goal. Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_message_feet.py`, a real server on a scripted model, a chat whose first message came with a file and
was answered and whose second works, is steered, and works on until it is stopped; at 1280 px light and dark and at
390 px: the earlier message's foot (its time, the full date where the pointer rests, the copy, Send again), the answer's
(the copy, the time, the run's length hidden until the pointer rests), no foot under the goal or the steering message
while the run works and both once it is stopped, each copy on the clipboard with its check, Send again starting the
chat's next run with the first message and its file and leaving the draft in the composer, the file between the message
and its foot, the icons at the bubble's edge, and the forms of the time. On the code of before, it found no foot. It
passed in WebKit too.

**What.** Under each of the owner's messages that has its answer: the time it was sent (the day too when it was not
today, the full date where the pointer rests), a copy of the message as it was written, and a button that sends it again
to the same chat, with the files it carried. Under each answer: its time and a copy, an icon each.

### 206. Markdown in the conversation, and copies that keep it

**Status: done.** Merged as `33a7f8d` (PR #245; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** The owner's messages are drawn by the answers' reader (`prose.js`): a goal, a message that
steered a run and an earlier turn read as markdown, with their headings, lists, quotes, tables, code, emphasis and web
links, and the line breaks as typed; in the bubble, code and the heads of a table sit one surface up from it. A copy out
of the conversation keeps its markdown (`clipboard.js`): a selection that starts in a message or an
answer goes on the clipboard as the markdown it was written in, read back from copies of the selected nodes. Headings
come back at the level they were written at (`data-level`; Dot draws them one level down), with lists, quotes, fenced
code (its fence longer than any run of backticks in it), inline code, bold, italic, web links (an address that repeats
its words stays bare), tables with their pipes escaped and a row of dashes under the first, and rules. A file's path, a
button, copies as its code; the other buttons, the faces, the line under a message or an answer and what only a screen
reader hears stay out. A selection across the items of a list or the rows of a table keeps its list or table; one within
a line keeps its marks. The formatted copy goes along as clean HTML for the applications that read it: of the attributes
only a web link's address stays, and it is serialized from the nodes, never built from a string. A copy within one block
of code, or out of the composer, is the browser's own. The composer's
part is item 207. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_markdown_copy.py`, a real server, a chat of two turns whose first message
holds a table and a list and whose answer holds every kind of block and mark; at 1280 px light and dark and at 390 px:
the message's table, list and marks, a whole answer copied back to the text it was written in, the message with its
answer without their feet and the face, two items of a list and two rows of a table as a list and a table, the marks
within a line, the browser's own copy within code and out of the composer, the HTML without classes, data or buttons,
and a real ⌘C to the clipboard in Chrome. On the code of before, it found no table in the message. It passed in WebKit
too.

**What.** The owner's messages are read as markdown, as the answers are (headings, lists, tables, code, emphasis). A
copy of a part of the conversation keeps its markdown: the text carries the markdown, and the
formatted copy goes along for the applications that read it. The copy buttons copy the markdown as written.

### 207. The composer shows the markdown it holds

**Status: done.** Merged as `23f1d9a` (PR #246; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** Not a rich text editor that hides the marks it reads: Dot's box stays a
text field, which the slash menu, the files, the queue, the drafts, the keys, the listening face and the send all use,
and shows its markdown from under it (`mirror.js`): a copy of the box's text lies under the box in the same room, letter
for letter, and the box's own letters are clear over it, so the caret, the selection (the system's colour, light enough
to read through), the spelling, an input method and the undo stay the text field's own. Each line of the copy is read as
`parseBlocks` and `parseInline` read it (`sourceLines` in `markdown.js`, which keeps every character in its place): a
heading's hashes, a list's mark, a quote's >, the stars of bold and italics, the backticks of code, a link's brackets
and address, a table's pipes and the dashes under its head, a fence and a rule show quieter than the words; bold words,
headings and a table's head heavier; inline code and the lines of a block of code tinted; quotes softer; links in the
colour of links. The marks are read within one line, so bold or code that runs over a line break shows plain in the box,
though the conversation shows it as written. Nothing in the copy changes a letter's size or width, or it would set its
letters elsewhere than the box: headings keep the size of the text and italics stay upright, weight is a stroke on a
whole line and a shadow on a bold word, and the marks within a line are highlights of the line's one text (the CSS
Custom Highlight API), not elements, since a line cut into elements sets its letters a fraction of a pixel apart from
the box's (0.1 px over a line in Chrome, 0.3 px in WebKit), enough to wrap a word elsewhere. The box and its copy sit in
a field that is a column, as the composer is, so the composer is no higher for the copy. The copy scrolls with the box,
leaves the room of its scroll bar, and paints again on every change of the text: typing, a paste, a pick of the slash
menu, a draft brought back, an edit of the queue, a send. A browser without highlights (before Chrome 105 or Safari
17.2) shows the lines' kinds without the marks' colours; with the system's colours forced, the box shows its own
letters. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_composer_markdown.py`, a real server; at 1280 px light and dark and at 390 px: every
kind of line and mark in the new chat's box; the copy holding the box's text after typing, a pick of the slash menu, a
draft brought back by a reload and a paste; and the pixels: the copy in one colour and the box's own letters differ in
no more than 0.1 % of the box, in the new chat's box and in a chat's dock scrolled half way and to its end (a copy one
pixel off differs in 2 %), while the copy as it shows differs from the copy in one colour; the field is as high as the
box in it (5 px higher before it was a column). On the code of before, it found no copy. It passed in WebKit too.

**What.** The composer keeps the markdown it holds and shows it styled: headings as headings, emphasis, code, lists,
quotes, fences, rules and tables' pipes, their marks faded. A paste of markdown shows at once
in that order. What is sent is the markdown, as now; the slash menu, the files, the queue, the drafts and the keys work
as before.

### 208. The model menu: providers at the side, a search and favourites

**Status: done.** Merged as `2545d60` (PR #247; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** The Model pill's menu is made of Dot's own parts (`modelpicker.js`): a
rail on its left with the favourites' star, a rule, then the mark of each provider that lists models that can call
tools, its name where the pointer rests; the view shown is pressed, with a bar on the rail's edge. A provider's view
lists its models in the order the provider gives them, the favourites' view lists the favourites with their providers'
names, and the daemon's default stays the first row of every view. The search above the list takes the keys as the menu
opens (where a pointer can hover; on a touch screen it leaves the focus where it is, so that no keyboard springs up over
the list) and looks across every provider: each word has to be in the model's name, its provider's name or id, or
"free"; a name counts before a provider and a whole word or a start before the middle, the favourites go first on a tie,
then the providers' order; while it searches the rail presses none, and a search that finds nothing says so. Each model
has a star that keeps it among the favourites without picking it. The favourites are kept in this browser, as the home's
choices are (`dot.models.favourites`, read back only as a list of references), and the menu opens on them once one of
them is offered, else on the provider of the model a run would use (a menu opened before the models or the daemon's
default had come chooses again once they come); a row starred or unstarred stays in its place until the list is shown
again. The keys stay in the search: the arrows move the row they are on (the tint; the chosen model has its tick), Enter
picks it, ⌘1 to ⌘9 pick the first nine models of the list, which show those keys, ⌘D stars the row the keys are on, the
left arrow on an empty search or Shift+Tab goes to the rail (up and down there, Enter shows a view, the right arrow goes
back) and Escape closes the menu; a press on a row or a star leaves the keys in the search. The menu keeps one height
whatever it shows, so a view never moves its top, and only the list scrolls. `popover.js` lets a control of a panel take
the focus as it opens (`data-autofocus`) and keep the arrows it answers itself; the providers' headings of the old list
(`.pop-group`) went with it. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_model_picker.py`, a real server whose providers list the test's
models (stand-ins for OpenAI and Anthropic, which answer nothing; a model that cannot call tools and a provider with no
key are left out): the rail and its marks, the opening view, a provider's view, searches across providers (one for a
free model, one that finds nothing), a star that picks nothing and is kept, the arrows and Enter, the favourites' view
and ⌘1, ⌘D, the rail by the keys, Escape and the default's row; at 1280 px light and dark and at 390 px, and on a touch
screen, where the search takes no focus and the rows show no keys; and a menu opened while the model list was held back,
which moves to its opening view once the list comes. On the code of before, it found no picker. It passed in WebKit too,
and the tests of the composer's other menus pass unchanged.

**What.** The composer's model menu gets a rail of the providers' marks at its left (favourites first), which filters
the list to one provider; a search over every provider's models; a star on each model that keeps it among the
favourites; and keys: the arrows and Enter, ⌘1 to ⌘9 for the rows in sight.

### 210. The shell check: changes of permissions

**Status: done.** Merged as `34f4816` (PR #249; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** The shell check judges a change of permissions or of owner (`chmod`, `chown`, `chgrp`) by
every path the line names. It set the first word after the options aside as the mode or the owner, after the words that
are numbers had already been left out, and a mode can start with "-" like an option, so the word set aside was not
always the mode. Now no word is set aside: a number is still left out, and a mode or an owner that is no number is
judged as a path in the line's own folder, which never makes the line milder than the paths beside it. Tests:
`tests/unit/test_shell_policy.py`, ten lines: a change of a system file's permissions or owner asks (a mode as a number,
as letters or starting with "-", recursive or not), one of a protected file is refused, and one in the workspace runs,
as before. On the code of before, five of them were judged too mildly.

**What.** The shell check judges a change of permissions by every path it names.

### 211. Secrets kept from the agent by default

**Status: done.** Merged as `e6c8185` (PR #250; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** The places the agent can neither read nor change by default (`[policy] protected_paths` in
`defaults.toml`) hold more of those where a Mac keeps credentials and private data: the tokens and passwords command
lines keep for their hosts and registries (`~/.netrc`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.config/gh`, `~/.npmrc`, `~/.pypirc`,
the credentials of Cargo and RubyGems, `~/.docker/config.json`, `~/.kube`, `~/.azure`, `~/.config/op`,
`~/.password-store`), the shell's history, Messages, Mail, the cookies, and the data of Safari, Firefox, Brave, Edge and
Arc. Commands such as `git` and `gh` still read their own credentials; a line or a file tool that names these places is
refused. A list of one's own in `config.toml` replaces the default one, as before, which the README now says. Dot's own
reading of a code from Messages goes on: it opens the database itself, not through the agent's tools. Tests:
`tests/unit/test_shell_policy.py`, eleven lines that read from these places are refused with the default list; on the
code of before, all eleven were allowed.

**What.** More of the places where credentials are kept are protected by default.

### 212. A provider that is not running answers at once

**Status: done.** Merged as `d6f90eb` (PR #251; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** A server on this Mac (`localhost` or a loopback address) is asked for its list of models once
(`llm/ollama.py`): with no network in between, a refused connection means it is not running, so the model menu's list
and `dotx models` fail at once instead of after the retries of the call (about half a minute; the doctor took about two
minutes, as it asked each configured model in turn). A chat and a run's lookup of a model keep their retries, and so
does the list of a server elsewhere (ollama.com, another machine). The doctor (`doctor.py`) asks nothing more of an
Ollama server it could not reach at all: each model row (`main`, `vision`, `fast`, `review`, helpers, standby) is a
warning that says why, and the memory row (with Ollama's embeddings) fails with the server's reason, beside the
server's own failing row; a server that answers wrongly is still asked.
The plan's checks side by side within a time limit were not needed once nothing waits. Tests: a new test in
`tests/smoke/test_doctor.py`, with the Ollama server at a port of this Mac where nothing listens and the real
connectors: the list fails at once and the doctor's rows say why, within 10 s (it took 0.2 s); on the code of before it
was cut at 10 s, the retries still going.

**What.** When a provider's app is not running (Ollama on this Mac), the model list and the health checks say so at once
instead of trying again for half a minute.

### 213. Tests: a bare pytest, and every offline smoke test in CI

**Status: done.** Merged as `e73a257` (PR #252; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** `pyproject.toml`: each test module is imported by its path (`--import-mode=importlib`), as
`tests/unit` and `tests/smoke` have modules of the same name, and a smoke test that borrows from another finds it on
`tests/smoke`; a mark that is not registered fails (`--strict-markers`), so a mistyped one cannot pick a test that needs
a service. A bare `pytest` collects all 1,854 tests without an error (19 errors before). CI (`gate.yml`) runs every
smoke test that needs no service, chosen by its marks (not `live`, `browser`, `internet`, `desktop` or `hosted`),
instead of a list of 22 files: 312 passed and 1 skipped on this Mac in 2 min 36 s. The smoke tests that drove a browser
or a model without saying so got their marks, 12 `browser` and 14 `live` in 11 files. The model menu's test waits for
the providers' rail, which it once read before the daemon had listed them.

**What.** A bare `pytest` collects every test without an error, and CI runs every smoke test that needs no service,
chosen by their marks instead of by a list of files.

### 214. The redactor knows more kinds of secrets

**Status: done.** Merged as `3347d33` (PR #253; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** The redactor (`core/text.py`, `redact_secrets`), which masks what goes into the log, the
events, the errors the API answers with and the lessons, knew keys that start with `sk-`, bearer tokens and the value of
`key=value` under a few names. It now knows the keys and tokens of GitHub, an AWS access key id, a Google API key,
Slack's tokens and a JSON web token by the forms their services give them; a private key in PEM; the credentials of a
Basic Authorization header; the password of a URL, keeping the rest of it; and the value of `key=value` or
`"key": "value"` under more names, a password's however short. What surrounds a secret is kept, words that only look
like one are left alone, and no pattern tries a long run of words against the whole rest of the text. Tests:
`tests/unit/test_redaction.py`, 19 made-up secrets (those in the form of a real service's key put together at run time),
9 look-alikes and a long text; on the code of before, 14 of the 19 stayed in the text.

**What.** The redactor that keeps secrets out of logs, lessons and errors knows more kinds of them.

starts with Homebrew's folders. An IPv6 address that carries an IPv4 one is judged by it in each form that carries one

### 216. The README says what leaves this Mac

**Status: done.** Merged as `b8d6f34` (PR #255; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** The README's opening paragraph sends the reader to a new section before Safety, What leaves

is what a run needs, where the configuration points: the run's conversation to the models (by default Ollama's cloud
models, through the Ollama server of this Mac), each note and search of the memory to the embedding model, the query to
the search engines, the requests to the sites a run visits, whatever a shell command sends, the texts TypeSafe judges
once its key is saved, a line to a phone whose notifications are on, and what the tools of MCP servers and plugins are
given. It ends with what stays on the Mac and how to keep a run's conversation here too. README only.

**What.** The README says in one place what leaves this Mac and where it goes: the models in the cloud by default, what
is sent to them, and how to keep it on the Mac.

### 217. A weekly audit of the dependencies

**Status: done.** Merged as `48772b2` (PR #256; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** `.github/workflows/audit.yml` checks the dependencies as locked against the public advisories
every Monday and when asked. On macOS, where PyObjC is among the requirements, `uv export` writes `uv.lock` as
requirements pinned with their hashes and pip-audit 2.10.1 checks them as they are, resolving nothing; cargo-audit
0.22.2 checks the desktop shell's `Cargo.lock` against the RustSec database. A known vulnerability fails the job, so
GitHub says so; nothing is changed or opened. The jobs' token can only read, and each action is pinned by its commit, as
in `gate.yml`. The same pip-audit on this Mac found no known vulnerability in the 86 pinned packages.

**What.** A weekly job checks the Python and Rust dependencies against the public advisories.

## Part 35: lists that keep a size, imports, the side panel's motion, models' windows, fast mode (planned 2026-10-14)

The owner's thirty-fourth word, on 2026-10-14: the list of skills on the Skills page should keep a size and scroll
inside past a point, and so should the notes of the Memory page; a button should import with ease the skills and
settings of the Mac's other apps, Claude Code, Codex and the others; the Screen tab could look better while it is empty,
and the side panel should open and close with a motion; every provider's models should show their context window right,
with a meter of it; and Claude's models that have fast mode, Ultracode or Ultrathink should offer them.

**Status (2026-10-14): planned.** Each was checked on the code first. Settings › Skills and Settings › Memory listed
every row on the page itself. The Skills page showed what the other agents set up with an Add for each, one at a time.
Beside the conversation the side panel came and went at once, and the Screen tab said in one grey line why it had no
frame. OpenAI's GPT-5.4 and 5.5, with their pro models, and the chat models of GPT-5.1 to 5.3 had other windows than
their pages publish, and Ollama's cloud models named as `name:size-cloud` were taken for models of this Mac. Nothing
showed how full a run's context was. Fast mode is a research preview of Anthropic's API for some Opus models, at twice
the price; Ultracode and Ultrathink are features of Claude Code, not levels of the API.

**The shape of this part (the decisions).** Six items, each a pull request of its own, after those of part 34. An import
adds only what the owner ticks in a checklist: the skills are ticked at first and the MCP servers not, as a server
starts a program of this Mac; tests read homes of their own, never the Mac's. The context meter measures the last step's
prompt against the run's budget, past which Dot summarizes, and names the model's window beside it; it asks nothing of
the model. Fast mode is off until the owner turns it on for a chat. Left to the owner, and asked: Ultracode and
Ultrathink, as the API has no such levels (Max is its deepest effort, and Dot's helpers and teams are its many agents).
Item 196 of part 31 still waits on the owner.

### 223. Claude's fast mode

**Status: done.** Merged as `a3ace6d` (PR #262; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** Claude Opus 5.5, Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 have fast mode: up to 2.5 times the output speed at
twice the price, a research preview. The Models API does not say which models have it, so `FAST_MODE_MODELS` in
`llm/anthropic.py` names them from Anthropic's page; a request in fast mode sends `speed: "fast"` with the beta
`fast-mode-2026-02-01`, and Dot never falls back to the standard speed by itself. The speed is kept like the reasoning
level, by the run, a chat's choices, a queued message and a campaign (those of before hold `standard`); each step of a
run in fast mode asks for it where the step's model has it, and summaries, reviews and the other calls run at the
standard speed. Fast mode for a model without it is refused (a 422 over HTTP). The Reasoning menu of such a model has
Speed, Standard or Fast, off at first; the pill then reads `High · Fast`. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_fast_mode.py`,
against a stand-in of Anthropic's API and in a browser, and `tests/unit/test_store_speed.py`; on the code of before, all
four fail. Not checked against Anthropic, as fast mode needs an organization let into the preview. Left to the owner:
Ultracode and Ultrathink, for which the API has no levels.

**What.** The Claude models that have fast mode offer it in the composer's reasoning menu, off by default, for a chat at
a time; the API's refusal is shown as it is.

## Part 36: helpers at a glance, previous agents, commands in the background (planned 2026-10-14)

The owner's thirty-fifth and thirty-sixth words, on 2026-10-14. The first: a helper's row should have
a card on hovering it that gives the helper's model, its reasoning level, how long it has run and what it is doing;
what is useful among another app's settings should come to Dot; and at the conversation's far left there should be the
rail of dashes that stands for each message and each session. The second, queued after the first: the side panel should
list the previous agents, and look better, with SVG icons; a run's lessons that could not be drawn as "the
review model did not call propose_lessons", and a summary's check that flagged a path under `~` as unverified, should be
fixed if they are faults; and a command that runs for hours, past the shell's limit of 30 minutes, should run in the
background, with Dot checking on it.

**Status (2026-10-14): planned.** Each was checked on the code first. A helper's row in the conversation showed its
title and its state; its model and reasoning level were kept but shown nowhere, and what it was doing showed only once
it was opened. The run page's side panel had no list of a chat's helpers. The rail of marks of item 201 hid itself when
less than 40 px was left at the conversation's left, as beside the docked side panel. Of that app's settings, Dot had
skills in the slash menu and a question before a delete; Enter always sent, a message to a busy run was always queued
(⌘⇧Enter steered it), runs went on after a restart only through `[agent] resume` in the config file, and Settings ›
Models showed the fast, review and vision models with no way to change them. The review model that draws a run's lessons
at times declined: Anthropic's API ended its reply as a `refusal`, with no call and no text, and Dot asked it once more
and then said it did not call `propose_lessons`. The check of a summary knew a path only as the history wrote it, so a
summary that wrote `~/…` for a path the history held under the home folder's full name was flagged. The shell ends a
command at its timeout, 30 minutes at most; a terminal session is closed after 30 minutes without a read, and nothing
told a chat that a long command had ended.

**The shape of this part (the decisions).** Nine items, each a pull request of its own, after those of part 35; the two
faults first. A refusal is said as it is and not asked again, and Dot does not turn to another model by itself: whether
the lessons should is left to the owner, who can choose the review model in Settings › Models (item 232). A command in
the background belongs to its chat: it outlives the run that started it but not the daemon, and its end is told to the
chat as a message. Of that app's other settings, Dot has what they do already or has no use for them; the list, with the
reasons, is in the report of this part. Item 196 of part 31 still waits on the owner.

> of part 5 (branch, gate, PR, Linear MYP issue when the connector is signed in, squash merge, hash in the table, log
> line) is unchanged. Give each change a test that fails on the code of before, and check a page that changes in a
> browser, wide and on a phone, light and dark. Tests never start a real model call or read the other agents' files
> of the Mac. Never touch the owner's data directory except to read it, by the kinds and numbers of what is stored,
> and to restart the daemon when `/api/status` shows no active run; PLAN.md stays untracked. The owner reads Turkish;
> everything written is English.

### 224. A summary's check knows a path however it is written

**Status: done.** Merged as `109c270` (PR #263; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** Before Dot replaces a run's older history with a summary, it checks that each path, address
and id the summary names is in the history it replaces, and a summary that names one that is not is flagged as
unverified. A path counted only as the history wrote it. It now counts in each of the ways a Mac writes it (`spellings`
in `agent/continuity.py`): `~` for the home folder and the home folder for `~`, and `/tmp` or `/var` with or without
`/private` before them; an address or an id is only itself. Tests: `tests/unit/test_continuity.py`, a summary that names
in one spelling three paths the history holds in another, and two paths the history holds in none; on the code of
before, the three are flagged.

**What.** The check of a summary that replaces a run's history knows a path in each of the ways a Mac writes it, `~` or
the home folder, `/tmp` or `/private/tmp`, and flags no path the history holds.

### 225. A model that declines is said to have declined

**Status: done.** Merged as `103f5b2` (PR #264; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** The review model answers Dot's own questions, each by a call of one tool, and a reply without
it is asked for once more. A reply its provider ends as a refusal (Anthropic's stop reason `refusal`, OpenAI's finish
reason `content_filter`) with no call is now a `ProviderRefusedError` (`core/errors.py`), raised at once and not asked
again, that names the model: "the review model … declined to answer (stop reason: refusal)". It is a `ProviderError`, so
the goal check, the second opinion, the lessons, the reflection and a rule's words handle it as they handled the model's
failures; Dot does not turn to another model by itself. Tests: `tests/unit/test_review_declined.py`, a stand-in model
whose replies end as a refusal, as filtered content, or with no call; on the code of before, the refusal and the
filtered reply were each asked twice and reported as a model that did not call `propose_lessons`.

**What.** When the review model declines, its provider ending the reply as a refusal, the lessons and the reflection say
so at once, instead of asking again and saying that the model did not use its tool.

**Status: done.** Merged as `3216c6f` (PR #270; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

## Part 37: what an eval run showed (planned 2026-10-15)

The owner's thirty-seventh word, on 2026-10-15: what an eval run showed. An error of the harness ended the run with four
tasks unplayed; two answers that refused an instruction hidden in a file, and only quoted it, were counted as having
followed it; one task failed where the model took, as its rules tell it, the smallest reasonable reading of the goal; a
yolo run reads secrets and sends data; and in a yolo run started from the web UI the agent's questions are not waited
for. The first two are faults to fix; for the other three the owner asked for a decision on how Dot should behave.

**Status (2026-10-15): planned.** Each was checked on the code and on the run's saved report first. `dotx eval run`
looked up the review model's key only with `[agent] goal_mode` or `stall_escalation` on, while the form task runs in
goal mode of its own; the attempt's throw-away home has no `.env` file, so its goal check could not run ("missing API
key"), and the event of a goal check that could not run lacked the count of unproven steps that the harness reads, which
ended the eval run. Since item 54 an attempt asked for goal mode only when its task did, so `[agent] goal_mode`, which
the report keeps as a setting of the run, changed nothing. Two of the three tasks that hide an instruction judged it
followed when the answer held words that the instruction itself holds, so an answer that quoted it while refusing it
counted as following it. The headlines task asked for the headlines "about electric cars" and expected those about their
batteries and their charging too; the model took the smallest reasonable reading, as the system prompt tells it when a
request can be read in several ways, and said so. The task's count check passed although the count was wrong, matching a
digit in a car's name, and nothing checked that the file held nothing else.

**The shape of this part (the decisions).** Three items, each a pull request of its own. The rule of the smallest
reasonable reading stays: it keeps Dot from widening a task, and the model did what it says, naming the reading it took;
the task changes instead, naming what it checks. A yolo run keeps what it does: the owner chooses it, the composer says
what it waives when it is chosen and the run carries a chip, `ask` stays the default, and a rule with the hand-off
behaviour still stops a yolo run at secrets, money and credentials. The agent's questions in a yolo run are not lost:
they are listed under "Dot asked you" on the run's page and in its timeline, during the run and after it, and an answer
reaches the conversation; nothing changes there. Item 196 of part 31 still waits on the owner.

### 233. Goal checks in an eval run

**Status: done.** Merged as `7c47b6c` (PR #272; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-15).** `dotx eval run` looks up the keys of the model under measure and of the fast, review and
vision models before the attempts' homes take over (`reached_models`), and does not start without the first, nor without
the review model's when an attempt checks the end of its run (`required_models`: `[agent] goal_mode`,
`stall_escalation`, or a task in goal mode, its own or by a goal that asks to keep going). An attempt asks for goal mode
when its task does and otherwise takes the configured one, as before item 54. A goal check that cannot run writes the
count of its unproven steps, none, as the other goal checks do. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_evals_runner.py`, a review
model whose key is nowhere: the attempt ends as failed with the reason, and is judged and counted;
`tests/unit/test_evals.py`, the models whose keys an eval run needs. On the code of before the attempt is not checked at
all, and an attempt at a task in goal mode of its own ends the eval run ("a goal check lacks the unproven steps the
harness counts").

**What.** An eval run hands each attempt the keys of every model it may call and needs the review model's whenever an
attempt checks the end of its run; `[agent] goal_mode` puts every attempt in goal mode again, as the report says; and a
goal check that cannot run ends its attempt as failed, saying why, while the eval run goes on.

## Part 38: imports, the prompt cache, the side panel, the run's budget (planned 2026-10-15)

The owner's thirty-eighth word, on 2026-10-15: an import from other apps failed with "an item is named more than once";
the context meter of a model that holds a million tokens shows a budget of 96,000; the side panel should stand at the
window's right edge; and after many features, speed, streaming, the agent's flow and ease of use had
not been reviewed.

**Status (2026-10-15): planned.** Each was checked on the code, and the cache on the owner's record of model calls of
the last four days, by kinds and numbers only. The import: Dot finds the skills of another agent's folder as it finds
its own, a few levels down, and one name can be there more than once (on the owner's Mac, 13 names, each 3, 7 or 9
times); the checklist offered each copy, and the import, which names an item by its agent and its name, refused the
whole request. A plugin installed for the user and for a project, or by two marketplaces, would do the same. The budget:
`[agent] context_tokens` is Dot's budget for a run's prompt, 96,000 tokens whatever the model's window (decision 33);
the meter gives both numbers but not why they differ. The cache: Anthropic step calls whose prompt was under 57,600
tokens (60 % of the budget, past which older tool output is shortened) read 63 to 71 % of it from the cache and took 5
to 12 s on average; above it, 184 of 291 calls, they read 2 to 3 % and took 35 s. Past that point each step shortens the
tool result that leaves the newest six, some 25 blocks before the end, while Anthropic looks for a cached prefix at most
20 blocks before a request's breakpoint, and Dot sets one breakpoint, at the end: so each such step reads the whole
prompt anew and writes it to the cache again, at 1.25 times the price of input. DeepSeek through OpenCode Go keeps 79 %
there, as its cache matches the part before a change. The panel: the run page keeps a reading width of 1,240 px while
the panel has its own width, so on a wide window the panel stands in the middle.

**The shape of this part.** Five items, each a pull request of its own: the import, which stops the owner, first; then
the cache, the largest cost measured; then the panel and the meter; last the fast model's pause, which the review found
in the side calls of the owner's runs. Found by the same review and left for a part of their own: a change of the open
plan, which sits at the end of the system prompt, misses the whole cache on every provider (8 of 291 Anthropic step
calls, 73 of about 2,100 OpenCode Go ones), and moving the plan to the end of the request would make each step a new
turn of the owner's, which a model that reasons may take differently, so it waits for an eval on real models; a summary
holds its run up while it is written (27.6 s on average on OpenCode Go). Measured and left as they are: a run page loads
the whole log of its run, on the owner's record at most 1,674 events and 1.2 MB; a step whose tools changed missed no
cache there; a reply's live text is set as plain text and drawn once at its end.

### 237. The prompt cache holds when old output is shortened

**Status: done.** Merged as `24194bf` (PR #277; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-15).** `ChatRequest.cache_mark` names the last message the next step sends unchanged. The loop gives
the one before the oldest of the newest `keep_recent_tool_results` tool results and `keep_recent_screenshots`
screenshots (`last_settled`, `agent/compact.py`), which a later step may still shorten or strip. The Anthropic connector
puts a cache mark on that message's last block besides the automatic one at the end (`settled_mark` in
`MessagesOptions`; OpenCode Go's messages route gets none, as it was not tried there), so the step after a shortening
reads the run before the newest results from the cache. Building it showed that `truncate_middle` put its mark of what
was dropped on top of the size it was given: a result shortened to 700 characters had 728, so each of the next two steps
shortened it again and changed it. The mark now fits in the size, and a result is shortened once. Tried on Claude Haiku
5.5 with two calls shaped as two steps past the elision point (13,110 and 13,572 tokens): both were accepted, and the
second read the 2,880 tokens before the mark from the cache. Tests: `tests/unit/test_cache_mark.py` makes two
consecutive steps past the elision point with the real trimming and encoding. The second changes the prompt 24 positions
before its end, out of reach of a mark at the end; the first step's mark is 4 positions before the second's, and the
prompt up to it is the same in both. Shortened output stays as it is when shortened again. On the code of before the
test does not import, and one result was rewritten three times (728, 726 and 726 characters).

**What.** A step's request to Anthropic marks, besides its end, the end of the part of the run that the next step sends
unchanged, before the newest tool results that may still be shortened. The next step reads that part from the cache, and
a shortening costs only the newest steps.

### 240. Dot's own work leaves a paused fast model out

**Status: done.** Merged as `87b5cfc` (PR #280; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-15).** `paused_model` (`agent/helpers.py`) gives a model the router has paused, with why and until
when. `_compact` (`agent/loop.py`) asks it first: a paused fast model that is not the run's own is left out, the run's
own model writes the summary, and the `compacted` event's `fast_problem` says that the fast model (rate limited until a
time) cannot answer now. `web_extract` (`tools/web.py`) asks it before each source and lists a source it did not read
with the same words. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_scaffold.py` (a fast model that answers with a rate limit is asked once in
a run of many compactions; 39 times on the code of before) and `tests/smoke/test_crawl.py` (two extractions of two
sources each ask it once; four times on the code of before).

**What.** A run's summary and `web_extract` leave the fast model out while the router has paused it after a quota,
rate-limit or key error: the run's own model writes the summary at once, and `web_extract` reads no source and says
until when the fast model cannot answer. Before, each asked it anyway and spent the connector's retries first: on the
owner's record of four days, 122 calls of the fast model failed on its rate limit, 19 to 31 s each (24.8 s at the
median), 107 of them within the pause of the one before, and each summary then took 27.6 s more on the run's own model.

The owner's thirty-ninth word, on 2026-10-15: a second review of Dot, made at `c5aeed3`, to be checked, and what holds

shown and reviewed in part. A run's taint, which says that content third parties can author is in its context and has an

and so does the run Dot starts in a chat to say that a command in the background ended, although that message is Dot's

and a steer restore trust, as before; playbooks are still learned from runs that read the web, as most are (4 of the 5
on the owner's Mac, from 19 of the 22 task runs that ended done).

**The shape of this part.** Three items, each a pull request of its own: the redactor first, as it is the smallest; then
the approval card and the reviewer; then the taint. None asks the owner more than before: the owner's messages start

### 243. A run that goes on from another keeps its taint

**Status: done.** Merged as `bbe607e` (PR #284; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-15).** Each `tool_result` event holds whether the run is tainted after it, and `run_queued` whether
the run starts so (`agent/executor.py`, `agent/manager.py`). `tainted_after` (`agent/gate.py`) reads it from the newest
of a run's `run_queued`, `tool_result` and `steer` events: a steer clears the taint, and an event stored before they
held it counts as untainted. A run starts as tainted as the run it goes on from (`RunManager._starts_tainted`): a
delegated run as its parent is now, as before; a resumed run as the run it resumes was when it was cut off; and the run
that tells a chat that its command in the background ended as the chat's last run ended. A message of the owner starts a
run untainted. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_taint_goes_on.py` plays a run that reads a terminal and leaves a command in the
background: the run that tells of its end asks before it saves a note, and so does a run resumed after a shutdown cut
off such a run, while a message of the owner saves its note without asking (on the code of before the first two saved it
without asking); `tests/unit/test_taint_events.py` reads seven sets of events.

**What.** A run's events say whether it was tainted: each `tool_result` after its result, and `run_queued` as the run
starts. A run that resumes another starts tainted when that one was at the cut, and so does a run Dot starts in a chat
to say that a command in the background ended, when the chat's last run ended tainted. A message of the owner starts a
run untainted and a steer clears the taint, as before.

counting on every second while one works; an approval a helper asks for opens its group. A row that ended shows the
start of its answer as one plain line (`plainLine`: no marks of headings, lists, bold or code, links as their words),
after how it ended unless it is done; a run with no answer says how it ended and in how many steps, as before. Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_helper_group.py` delegates four helpers in one step, three answering and one working, wide and on a
phone, light and dark, in Chrome and (copied for the check) in WebKit: one group, "4 helpers", "1 working · 3 done",
three faces and "+1", a time that counts on, rows with the start of their answers, a head that folds the rows away and
brings them back, "3 done · 1 stopped" once the working one is stopped, and the same group on the page loaded again; on
the code of before there is no group. `tests/smoke/test_helper_fold.py` reads the start of the answer where it read
"done".

**What.** Helpers whose rows follow one another sit in one group: a head with their
faces (three, then "+N"), how many they are, how they stand ("1 working · 3 done") and the time from the first one's
start to the last one's end, and a chevron that folds their rows away; the rows share one box. A row that is done shows
the start of its answer as one plain line.

### 246. Each step's thinking is a block that folds

**Status: done.** Merged as `5ef5a7b` (PR #287; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-15).** The `assistant` event keeps the step's thinking (`agent/loop.py`, `_THINKING_CHARS`): its
secrets masked, up to 12,000 characters, of a longer one its start and its end. `timeline.js` makes each step's thinking
a folded block (`startThought`) with the brain where a call has its icon: it grows as the thinking streams, says
"Thinking…" while the model thinks (a folded group of steps says so in its line) and "Thought" once it is done, the
start of the thought beside it. It is a row of the open group of steps; with none open, it stands at the end of the
conversation until the group its step's calls start takes it in as its first row, and that group opens with it when the
reader opened the thought. A group that ends before a call of the step comes, as the step writes a message or ends the
run, leaves the thought out of the fold, before the message or the answer (`liftThought`), and its line says its last
call again. The event's thinking stands for what streamed and makes the blocks of a page that reads the run afterwards,
in the same places. A step asked again from its start drops its block: one the connector asks again, as before, and now
one that `agent/loop.py` asks again (its routed model failed, its model could not be reached, or the run moved to a
standby model), which first streams the same reset, so the page also drops the text the failed try streamed. Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_thinking_blocks.py` streams the thoughts of three steps while the page follows the run: "Thinking…"
with the start of the first thought, which the reader opens and reads as it comes, then "Thought", the first row of its
step's group, which opened with it; the thought of the step that writes a message stands before it and that of the last
step before the answer, out of the groups; the events keep a short thought whole and of one of 21,489 characters its
start and its end; the page loaded again, wide and on a phone, light and dark, in Chrome and (copied for the check) in
WebKit, shows the blocks in the same places, folded, each opening to its thought and folding again, the long one
scrolling within its box. `tests/smoke/test_model_wait.py` sees a reset each time a step is asked again after its model
could not be reached. On the code of before there is no block and no such reset.

**What.** Each step's thinking is a block among the step's tool calls, a brain for its icon: "Thinking…" while the model
thinks and "Thought" once it is done, the start of the thought beside it; folded at first, it opens to the whole thought
and folds again. The `assistant` event keeps the thinking, its secrets masked, up to 12,000 characters (of a longer one
its start and its end), so a page loaded later shows it.

**What.** An MIT licence (`LICENSE`, and the `license` of `pyproject.toml`); a security policy (`SECURITY.md`) that

daemon cut off at most 30 minutes before, in calls that only read, goes on by itself when the daemon starts. `"off"`
leaves every such run to the owner, as before.

### 252. The plan at the end of the request, if an eval shows it holds

**Status: done.** Merged as `a786a28` (PR #296; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-15).** The A/B ran first, as the item says: a setting put the plan in a note after the conversation,
which no step stored, with the cache mark of the Messages format moved before the note, and `dotx eval run` played
`checklist-ten-files`, `digest-twelve-days`, `rename-helper-in-ten-modules`, `branch-totals-json`, `quarterly-report`
and `pipeline-with-flaky-stage` on OpenCode Go's DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with the plan in each place. The 18 attempts it
played before it was stopped all passed, and none kept a plan: the model does each of these tasks in 3 to 9 steps with
several calls a step, so both places sent the same requests (73.7 % and 75.5 % of the input from the cache) and the eval
could not tell them apart. The owner's runs of the last 30 days on that model measured what the place is worth: 19 of 26
task runs kept a plan, it changed 113 times in 2,346 steps, and the 77 steps right after a change took 14 % of their
input from the cache, against 77 % for the others. With the plan after the conversation those steps would read the cache
as the others do: about 2 points more of the input from the cache (75 % to 77 %), against the 15 the eval's design asked
for, while what a note after the conversation does to a thinking model's turn stayed unmeasured. So the plan stays at
the end of the system prompt, and the setting and the moved mark were not kept. What stays: `RunMetrics.plan_changes`
counts a run's plan events and a report says in how many attempts a plan was kept (`Scorecard.planned_attempts`, `-` for
a report saved before), so an eval of how the plan reaches the model shows whether its attempts planned. Tests:
`tests/unit/test_evals.py`.

**What.** An A/B eval of the plan at the end of the system prompt against the plan at the end of the request, on the
owner's main model, decides: the plan moves only if the share of cached input rises and the passes, the steps and the
plan steps marked done without evidence hold.

## Part 43: the plan of a provider, and the judge's switch (planned 2026-10-15)

The owner's forty-third word, on 2026-10-15: whether a key saved in Settings is the one in use when the models of a

`classify_generic` makes a plain `ProviderHttpError`: the model is not paused, every use of it fails again, and nothing

events, screen capture) are granted to the app that runs Dot, as the doctor reports; nothing is left to ask for. Claude's
fast mode stays as item 223 left it, off until the organization is let in; no item.

**The shape of this part.** Two items, each a pull request of its own: a model the plan does not include is paused at
once (254), and the typed judge switches on and off in Settings (255).

### 254. A model the plan does not include is paused at once

**Status: done.** Merged as `8e6cbfb` (PR #298; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-15).** `llm/provider_errors.py`: `classify_generic` makes a 402 a `ProviderQuotaError`, and
`classify_ollama` (the Ollama connector's classifier at its four sites) makes a 429 whose words say the included usage
is used up one too, the rest as before. `llm/router.py` `unavailable_reason` names a 402 "not in the plan". README:
the pause paragraph of the helpers. Tests: `tests/unit/test_provider_errors.py` (new) and `tests/unit/test_helpers.py`.

**What.** A provider's HTTP 402 (payment required: the plan does not include the model, or asks for credits) is a
`ProviderQuotaError` on every provider, terminal like a spent quota: the connector does not retry it, and the router
pauses the model for `helper_cooldown_s` with the reason "not in the plan", which the fast model's work (item 240),
the helpers and the standby read as they read a spent quota. Ollama's 429 that says the plan's included usage is used
up ("used all included") is a `ProviderQuotaError` too, through a classifier of Ollama's own; another 429 stays a rate
limit. README says so.

**Why.** The owner saved a new key and the models kept failing: each call to a model the plan does not include failed
again, nothing was paused and nothing said why. A paused model with its reason is what Settings, the timeline and the
doctor already show.

**Tests.** `tests/unit/test_provider_errors.py` (the 402 and the two 429s) and `tests/unit/test_helpers.py` (the pause
names the reason). They fail on the code of before.

**Status: done.** Merged as `b3cddbc` (PR #299; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-15).** `agent/judge.py` `SwitchedJudge`: the runtime's judge, with `provider` and `set_provider`,
answers through `TypeSafeJudge` while the provider is `"typesafe"` and through `NoJudge` otherwise; switching on
without the service raises a `ConfigError` that says to save the key and reinstall. `config.py` `JudgeProvider`;
`config_edit.py` `set_judge_provider` writes `[judge] provider`. `routes_system.py`: `GET` and `PUT /api/judge`
(`JudgeView`: provider, key name, whether the key is set) and the doctor's rows read the switch. `views/keys.js`: the

fast model out, with a `step_route_candidate_skipped` warning. README: the judge's paragraph. Tests:
`tests/unit/test_config_edit.py`, `tests/unit/test_judge.py` (the switched judge), `tests/smoke/test_judge.py` (the
paused fast model is not offered) and `tests/smoke/test_judge_switch.py` (the API, the config file, the doctor and the
Keys page in Chrome at 1280 and 390, light and dark; a WebKit copy).

(`"typesafe"` or `"none"`) into the config file and takes effect at once, with no restart, as the resume switch of
item 231 does: the runtime's judge answers through TypeSafe's service from the next judgment on, or answers nothing.

switching it on took a line in the config file and a restart. With the switch the owner tries it on their own runs and
turns it off when it does not help.

## Part 44: the levels that hold, the words in the box, and the quiet compaction (planned 2026-10-15)

The owner's forty-fourth word, on 2026-10-15: whether DeepSeek and Grok really support a choice like Ultrathink, and
that the levels offered must be true ones ("we cannot use what is not valid"); that typing ultrathink or ultracode in
the composer should be the choice for that message, the composer's border turning into a gradient while it is (a
screenshot of a composer with Ultrathink chosen: a green, orange and purple gradient around the box); whether
constant compaction harms long runs, and that the compaction notes should leave the conversation; that Excel and
OneDrive are now open; and, from the forty-third word and the report of part 43, a DeepSeek run that failed with a
`tokenize` error of the local Ollama runner, and that a schedule starting a fresh chat with the same prompt every day
repeats the same work. "Do whatever the best needs."

**Status (2026-10-15): planned.** On the code at `0250d88`, measured through the probe of part 43 on OpenCode Go
(counts only): the reasoning tokens of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash were the same at `low`, `high`, `max` and at a label that
does not exist (an easy prompt: 51, 53, 55 and 52; a harder one: 198 and 236 at low, 233 and 241 at max), while GLM 5.2
at `max` thought at length (453 reasoning tokens on the easy prompt); the gateway accepts any label for DeepSeek and
changes nothing. Grok 4.7 and GPT-6 Luna answer on the Responses route alone, which the probe did not
measure; their levels are the ones models.dev lists and the official client sends. The composer reads no word: the
choice for one message is the Reasoning menu's alone (item 251). The `compacted` event is a note in the timeline
("Context compacted: N earlier messages were summarised · by <model>"), one per compaction; over the last seven days the
owner's runs compacted 122 times in 26 runs (all by a model; the longest run 22 times; 9 checks flagged something). The run of a schedule starts a fresh thread each firing (`scheduler/runner.py`); a failed
embedding of the local Ollama runner (`/tokenize` reset) ends the run at its memory recall instead of being skipped.

**The shape of this part.** Five items, each a pull request of its own, in the order 258, 259, 260, 256, 257: the
levels (258) first, since the words of 259 are only as true as the levels behind them.

### 256. A failed embedding never fails a run

**Status: done.** Merged as `a9f8b68` (PR #303; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-15).** A run's start had two embedding calls without a guard: the recall of its notes and
the ranking of its skills by meaning (more skills than `[skills] listed`, `HelpVectors.closest`); the owner's run
failed after its notes were recalled, which leaves the second, and Ollama's 400 whose words are the failed
request to its runner was not retried. `core/errors.py`: `ProviderRunnerError`; `llm/provider_errors.py`:
`classify_ollama` makes a 400 or a 5xx one whose words are a request to the loopback that broke off (`runner_lost`,
reset, refused or EOF), and `llm/http.py` retries it as a broken connection; the embedder reads Ollama's answers with
`classify_ollama`. `agent/loop.py`: `_start_notes` recalls the notes by their words alone (`memory/service.py`
`words_only`) and `_close_skills` lists the skills by their words when the embedding service still fails, each with
an `embedding_failed` event and warning; `timeline.js` shows it as a warning line and `cli_ui.py` as a line of the
terminal. The memory's own calls (a save, a search of the tool) keep failing loudly, as tool errors the run reads.
README: the memory's search paragraph. Tests: `tests/unit/test_provider_errors.py` (the runner's 400 retried,
another 400 and a 404 with the runner's words not) and
`tests/smoke/test_embedding_failure.py` (new; a stand-in Ollama whose runner breaks off on every embedding).

**What.** A memory recall or a playbook match whose embedding call fails (the local Ollama runner reset, a `tokenize`
error, a connection reset) is retried once and then falls back to the text search, with a warning in the log
(`embedding_failed`) and the reason in the recall's event; the run goes on. The schedule's run that failed on 2026-10-15
at its `memories` event would have run.

**Why.** The owner asked why a DeepSeek run failed with `Post "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/tokenize": connection reset by
peer`: the run's model was fine; the embedding of its memory recall, on the local Ollama runner, failed and the failure
went uncaught.

**Tests.** A unit test of the recall with an embedder that raises (the text search answers, the warning is logged), and
a smoke test of a run whose embedder fails (the run ends done). They fail on the code of before.

### 260. The compaction notes leave the conversation

**Status: done.** Merged as `a8d8641` (PR #302; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-15).** `timeline.js`: the `compacted` handler counts the root run's compactions and the checks
that flagged something and tells `onCompacted({ count, flagged })`; no note. `views/run.js`: the counts are kept with
what the page has seen and painted into the Details. `details.js`: a Context fact ("Never compacted", "Compacted N
times", "N checks flagged"). README: the compaction paragraph. Test: `tests/smoke/test_quiet_compaction.py` (new),
with a WebKit copy run and deleted.

**What.** The timeline no longer shows a note for the `compacted` event: the conversation reads as the owner's messages
and the run's work. The event stays in the run's record and in the API; the Cost panel keeps the share of the summaries,
and the Details panel says how many times the run compacted its context and whether a check flagged anything, so what the
note said is still in sight, off the conversation. README says where it moved.

**Why.** The owner asked that the compaction notes not be shown in the conversation. On the frequency: a compaction
summarises the older part past `context_summarise_share` of the configured size and keeps the pinned ledger (goal, plan,
owner's messages, paths touched) whole, so a long run loses the detail of its oldest tool results, not its course; the
counts above are the measure. A wider context size for the model (item 250, Settings › Models) compacts less and costs
more a step; the choice is the owner's.

**Tests.** A smoke test of a run with a `compacted` event: no note in the conversation, the count in the Details panel.
Fails on the code of before.

### 263. A run runs JavaScript in its own tab

**Status: done.** Merged as `24a22d2` (PR #307; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-15).** `browser/driver.py`: `run_script` evaluates the script with Playwright's `page.evaluate`
within the time the call names and tells apart a value (its JSON, `null` for none), an error (the message without
Playwright's prefix and the lines of the call stack), a wait that ended first and a navigation that ended the script;
a tab closed under it is a `BrowserError`. `browser/session.py`: `BrowserSession.run_script` runs it in the thread's
own tab under the thread's lock, lets a page it led to load, holds the address rules after it as after a step (a
forbidden address resets the tab and fails the call) and says what else happened (`describe_surprise`).
`browser/types.py`: `ScriptRun`. `browser/render.py`: `render_script_run` (a line per end, the value cut in the
middle to the page budget, fenced as the page's). `tools/browser.py`: `browser_eval` (`script` up to 100 000
characters, `timeout_s` 30 by default and 1 to 600; acting modes only; a `browser_click` of medium risk on the tab's
page; the result marked untrusted, a thrown error and a timeout failures; its descriptions kept short, about 200
tokens, since a run that is sent every tool carries them at every step). `tools/apple.py`: `apple_script`'s
description sends a web page to `browser_eval`, as a script sent to Chrome reaches whichever Chrome window macOS
picks; the system prompt is unchanged. README (the tool table, the browser section). Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_browser_eval.py` (new; local pages in Dot's headless Chrome and in a scratch Chrome attached: the
value of an expression, a function and a promise, two threads each in its own tab, an error and a timeout told apart
with the page usable after both, a navigation let land and told, a forbidden address resetting the tab; and through a
run's tools on a real runtime, the classification under the three presets, the tool missing from research runs, the
value fenced and untrusted, a thrown error a failure). They fail on the code of before.

**What.** A browser tool, `browser_eval`, runs a script in the page of the run's own tab (Dot's Chrome or the owner's)
and returns its value: an expression, a function, or a promise it waits for, up to a time the call names. A script that
throws fails the call with its message; one that outlasts the time fails saying it may still run in the page. The value
comes back as page content (fenced, untrusted); the address rules hold after the script as after any step. It is
classified as a click that may change the page, at medium risk, as the shell guard rates the same script sent through
AppleScript: the cautious preset asks, the others do not, a research run cannot use it.

**Why.** The run had to reach the page through AppleScript, which lands in the wrong Chrome when several run, and could
do in one call what took a hundred.

**Tests.** A smoke test on a local page in Dot's Chrome and in the scratch Chrome attached: the value of an expression,
of a function and of a promise, two runs each in its own tab, an error, a timeout, a script that leads to a blocked
address; its classification under the presets. As built.

### 267. The phone reaches Dot from anywhere, and its home-screen app signs in with a code

**Status: done.** Merged as `a8c5cb0` (PR #313; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-15).** `server/pairing.py` (new): a code of eight characters of Crockford's base32 (40 bits), shown
as two groups of four and read back in any case, with or without the dash, O as 0 and I or L as 1; good for ten minutes
and once, five wrong tries use it up (`new_code`, `redeem`, pure). `server/routes_phone.py` (new): `GET /api/phone` (the
addresses, `https://` each name of `[server] reach`), `POST /api/phone/pairing` (a new code in place of the one before,
held in memory only) and `POST /api/phone/pair` (the token for the good code; `PairingRefused`, 403, otherwise, so that
the page's lost-token path does not run). `server/guard.py`: the pair route takes no token, while the Host and Origin
checks hold for it. `views.py`, `core/errors.py`, `app.py`. `api.js`: `pairWithCode` sends the code alone and brings
back the token, which is then proven as any other. `main.js`: the sign-in screen takes a pairing code first, says where
it is, and still takes the token. `views/phone.js` (new), `settings.js`, `icons.js` (smartphone), `settings.css`:
Settings › Phone, the steps with the address to copy and Pair a phone, the code large, until when it is good, and that
the Mac must be awake. The code and the token are never logged. README: Dot on the phone and the API table. Tests:
`tests/unit/test_pairing.py` (new) and `tests/smoke/test_phone_pairing.py` (new; through the API a code needs the token
to be given and none to be traded, is traded once as a person types it, five wrong tries and a newer code use it up,
another site's page is turned away; in Chrome a page on the Mac gets a code from Settings › Phone and a phone with no
token is let in with it after a wrong one is told, wide and on a phone, light and dark, and once in WebKit). The smoke
tests fail on the code of before.

**What.** Settings › Phone lists the address a phone reaches Dot at and gives a pairing code: a one-time code of a few
characters, good for minutes and limited in tries, which the sign-in screen of a phone's app trades for the token. What
the plan also named for this item, the state of Tailscale, setting it up with one button, a QR code and keeping the Mac
awake, is item 271.

**Why.** The QR code works in Safari, but the app on the home screen asks for a token nobody can type on a phone.

**Tests.** As built.

**Status: done (`5fcee1b`).** The owner chose it on 2026-10-17 for this round, with 268, 280 and 281. **As built
(2026-10-17).** `tailnet.py` reads Tailscale's command line, the app's own before one on the PATH (`tailscale status
--json`, `tailscale serve status --json`, its JSON validated), and `awake.py` holds macOS's `/usr/bin/caffeinate -s -w
<daemon pid>`. Settings › Phone › Reach Dot from anywhere says whether Tailscale runs signed in and the Mac's name,
whether it serves this daemon's port at `https://<name>/`, whether Dot answers to the name, the config file naming it
already when the daemon has not taken it up, and what Tailscale said when it could not be asked (its app closed, a call
that failed); **Set up** runs `tailscale serve --bg <port>` and writes the name into `[server] reach` (`config_edit`
writes a list now), one press at a time, and says that the daemon answers to it from its next start (`dotx service
install`): taking a name up without a restart would change the guard (`server/guard.py`), which is left as it is. **Keep
this Mac awake while it charges** (`[server] keep_awake`) starts and stops the hold at once and with the daemon, and a
config file that cannot be changed leaves it as it was. The tailnet name is never logged. Left out: the QR code of the
signed-in address, which would put the token on the screen; the pairing code signs a phone in. Tests:

`caffeinate` that `DOT_TAILSCALE` and `DOT_CAFFEINATE` name, every other smoke test naming ones that do not exist: the
state, Set up pressed twice at once and again, the switch on and off, a config file that cannot be changed, a Mac
without Tailscale, a Tailscale whose app is closed, whose answer cannot be read or whose command line cannot start, a
serve that waits ended in time with what it said; the card wide in Chrome and on a phone in WebKit, light and dark).
Docs: `docs/phone.md`, `docs/daemon.md`. On the owner's Mac after the merge, the daemon read Tailscale's status as
unreadable: run by a process with no terminal, as under launchd, the app's own program tries to start its window and

so).

**What.** Settings › Phone shows whether Tailscale runs, whether the daemon is served on the tailnet and whether
`[server] reach` names it, sets up what is missing with one button (reach taken up without a restart), shows the
signed-in address as a QR code, and offers to keep the Mac awake while it charges, so that the phone reaches Dot away
from home.

**Why.** Split from item 267, which made the phone's app sign in; the owner's Mac was set up by hand meanwhile.

**Tests.** The state read from a stand-in for the Tailscale command; the screen wide and on a phone, light and dark.

way. A structure after the three sayings, since Dot is to take part in coding, research, computer use and browser use
besides working around the clock, and may one day have a computer of its own in a cloud. On the phone the page slides
sideways and zooms; it is to hold still and fit every phone. In the app added to the home screen the sidebar's Settings
seems to go off the screen. On the phone something starting "The view" shows an error. The top bar always in place on
the phone.)

The three sayings, as the pictures give them: "Try using loops. I don't talk to an agent anymore. I talk to a loop, or I
talk to a routine, and it prompts Claude for me." (`/loop`) "Give Claude less context. Give it the minimal possible
system prompt, the minimal possible tools, and then you let the model figure it out." (`/context`) "Be open to being
wrong. I'm actually wrong so often now. So much of this engineering stuff that I've learned over the years I just have
to throw out." (`/rewind`) The fourth picture: every chat a coloured creature with two eyes, its name in bold and its
last message in grey under it, a blue dot at the right while it is unread; at the foot, the owner's picture and a
Connect apps pill with three small application icons.

What probes and a survey of the code measured the same day:

- In WebKit as an iPhone SE, 13 and 14 Pro Max and in Chrome as a Pixel 7, the meta viewport and touch on, the page
  slides sideways on Settings › Models alone: 51 px at 320 px, 9 px at 390 px. WebKit draws a select's chosen label past
  the select's box (`appearance: none`) and counts it in the row's overflow, 342 px in a row of 262; Chrome clips it.
- Text fields under 16 px, which iOS zooms the page into when they get the focus: the names of Settings › General
  (14 px), the model selects (13 px), the sign-in's code and token fields (13 px), the searches, and every other input,
  select and textarea but the composer's box.
- No safe area is used: the meta viewport has no `viewport-fit=cover` and no rule reads `env(safe-area-inset-*)`. The
  app added to the home screen runs to the screen's edges, so the sidebar's foot, Settings and the emergency stop 8 px
  from the bottom and the left, sits in the rounded corner and under the home indicator.
- The top bar is sticky and stays at the top as the page scrolls; iOS's rubber band at the top and its keyboard, which
  pans the page without resizing it, take it out of sight.
- "The view" is the toast "The view of Dot's computer stopped: …" of `computer.js`: the live view of the run's browser is
  a stream that, unlike the run's own, is not made again when it breaks, as iOS breaks every stream of a page put in the
  background.
- A chat in the sidebar is a status dot, its title and its age. Agents have a look (8 shapes, 12 colours, 16
  expressions); a chat has none, and no last message; unread is yes or no (item 131).
- Apps: no connector and no OAuth. MCP servers are set in `config.toml` alone, with no page to add, try or remove one;
  keys are for model providers; the Mac's applications are driven through AppleScript; My Chrome lends the owner's
  signed-in browser (item 261).
- Context: a task run's first step carries a system prompt of 25,591 characters and 57 tool schemas of 45,348, about
  22 k tokens at the loop's 3.2 characters a token. Tool groups exist (`tool_surface = "grouped"`, `use_tools`), but the
  default is "full" until evals show that groups help.
- Loops: schedules (cron or once), campaigns (sessions that plan the next until a check accepts the outcome) and goal
  mode (a checker sends a run back to work); a chat cannot be a loop.
- Rewind: the file tools' writes can be taken back per run and file (item 8); nothing rewinds a chat, forks it or edits a
  sent message.

A computer of Dot's own in a cloud is not planned: commands, the browser and the desktop are called on the Mac directly,
and such a machine would first need the one seam where work runs. Until the owner asks for it, items keep that seam in
mind and do not tie new work to the Mac where they need not.

**Status: done.** Merged as `d332e29` (PR #317; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-15).** `index.html`: `viewport-fit=cover`. `app.css`: `--safe-top`, `--safe-right`,

(`shell.css`), the sidebar's foot, the stage turned sideways, the composer's dock, the side panel as a drawer
(`run.css`) and the toasts; on `html`, `touch-action: manipulation` and `overscroll-behavior: none`; on a phone and on
any touch screen every input, select and textarea at least `--touch-text` (`max(16px, 1em)`), the composer's box
keeping its own size over it; a select clips its chosen label (WebKit drew it past the box and counted it in the row's
width, so Settings › Models slid 51 px on an iPhone SE); a note breaks a path or a command too long for its line
(Settings › API keys slid 143 px). `layout.js`: `holdBarInSight` moves the bar down by the visual viewport's offset,
which iOS's keyboard pans, so the bar stays at the top of what is seen. README: the phone. Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_phone_fit.py` (new): in WebKit as an iPhone SE and an iPhone 17 Pro Max and in Chrome as a Pixel 7,
the meta viewport and touch on, no page slides sideways and no text field is under 16 px on Activity, the new chat, a
run whose message holds a long link, a long line of code, a wide table and a long word, Agents, Campaigns, the eleven
Settings tabs, the sidebar open and the sign-in; with an iPhone's safe areas set (47 px at the top, 34 at the bottom),
the bar, the sidebar's head, Settings in its foot, the composer and the side panel keep out of them; a pan of the visual
viewport by 300 px takes the bar 300 px down and back. They fail on the code of before: fields of 14 px (the search of
the chats first), `touch-action: auto`, the bar at 0 under the top safe area, and the bar left behind by the pan.

**What.** The page uses the screen's safe areas (`viewport-fit=cover`; the bar, the sidebar's foot, the composer and
the side panel keep out of the rounded corners and the home indicator, through `--safe-*` tokens over
`env(safe-area-inset-*)`). Every text field is at least 16 px on a phone and on any touch screen, so iOS never zooms
into one; a double tap does not zoom (`touch-action: manipulation`); no page slides sideways (a select clips its label);
the page does not stretch at its ends (`overscroll-behavior: none`); and the top bar stays at the top of what is seen,

top of the seen page while the keyboard pans it.

### 276. The view of Dot's computer comes back by itself

**Status: done.** Merged as `f7e09a6` (PR #318; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-15).** `api.js`: `watchInView` reads a stream whose events stand alone while the page is in view:
out of sight it closes the stream and waits for the page to come back; a stream that breaks, or that `sse` cuts after
45 s of silence, is made again after the pause `follow` takes (0.5 s, doubling to 8 s, the shortest again once a stream
is taken); a refused stream (401, 404) ends the read with the error, as in `follow` (`refused`, shared with it); a fault
in showing one frame is told as in `follow`. `computer.js`: the view reads its screencast through it, so only a refused
stream ends it with the toast "The view of Dot's computer stopped"; before, any break or silence of the stream did, and
a phone breaks or stalls a page's streams whenever the app is put away. README: Dot's computer. Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_takeover.py` (one new test): in Chrome and in WebKit at a phone's width, the view's stream broken at
the network once and then silent until the page's clock jumps 46 s (a phone put away and taken up again) is made again
with no toast and shows the frame of the third stream; watched again and put out of sight, no stream is asked for while
out of sight, even past the stall, and the next comes once the page is back. It fails on the code of before (no second
stream is asked for) and with the wait for the page taken out (a fifth stream is asked for while out of sight).

**What.** The live view of the run's browser is made again when its stream breaks or goes silent, after the same pause
as the run's own stream, with no toast; it stops while the page is out of sight and starts again when it is back. A
stream the daemon refuses (the run is gone, the token is wrong) ends as today.

**Why.** The owner's ask: on the phone a toast starting "The view" shows an error whenever the app comes back.

**Tests.** Smoke: the view's stream broken once, and once silent; no toast, the next frame shown.
