### 279. Connect apps: the tools of other services, over MCP, signed in from Dot

**Status: done.** Merged as `8aa45dd` (PR #322; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What.** The same page lists the MCP servers Dot has, with their state and tools, and adds one from a short catalogue of
services that offer one (Notion, Linear, GitHub, Atlassian, Asana, …) or by its address or command: Dot tries it, and a
server that asks for a sign-in gets it in the browser (OAuth with PKCE, as MCP's authorization asks), the tokens kept
with Dot's keys and renewed; a server can be removed.

**Why.** The owner's ask; the services that offer tools over MCP are the shortest way to many applications.

**Tests.** Unit: the authorization's steps against a scripted server. Smoke: a server added, tried, listed with its
tools, removed.

**As built (2026-10-15).** `mcp/signin.py`: the MCP library's own flow (`OAuthClientProvider`: discovery, dynamic
client registration as a client without a secret, PKCE, renewal), over a file per server in `mcp-sign-ins/` (mode
0600: the tokens, the client, the redirect address it was registered with, when the token runs out, which the library
is told again at a start so that it renews a token that ran out while Dot was stopped). `SignIns.flow` is the owner's
sign-in from a page: the authorization server's page goes to the page, and the code comes back through
`GET /oauth/callback`, outside `/api` so that it needs no token, matched by its `state`; `kept_sign_in` is the runs':
the kept tokens and never a new sign-in, a server that asks for one being left out with `SIGN_IN_AGAIN`.
`McpConnection` takes the sign-in (`auth`, on the streamable HTTP client and on SSE), and an error of Dot's own sign-in
or of the library's flow is said as such instead of a refused connection. `McpHub` keeps its servers' configs and
connects (`connect`) or removes (`disconnect`) one while Dot runs, `attempt` tries one once; `refresh_mcp_tools` makes
the registry's MCP tools the hub's, for the runs that start after (a run's tools are its own copy). `McpServerConfig`
has `oauth`. `mcp/connected.py`: `connected-servers.json`, the servers added on Connect apps, connected at the start
after the config's, the plugins' and the other agents' (a name one of those has leaves one out, logged).
`mcp/catalogue.py`: Notion, Linear, Sentry, Cloudflare, Stripe and Todoist, which sign in, and DeepWiki and Microsoft
Learn, open to all, each checked in its authorization server's own metadata on 2026-10-15 (dynamic registration and a
client without a secret); GitHub (a personal token only), Asana, Slack, Google and Box (clients registered by hand),
Vercel, Figma, Canva and Atlassian (approved clients or allow-lists) are not in it, and Supabase and Hugging Face
register clients with a secret alone, not checked yet. `server/routes_mcp.py`: `GET /api/mcp/servers` (every server
with where it is set up, its state, tools, error and sign-in page; the services), `POST /api/mcp/servers` (a service,
or a name and a URL or command line; tried in a task of its own with a sign-in from the page's origin, which must be an
address of this server, and answered once the sign-in page is known, the try ended or 20 s passed; kept and connected
as runs connect once it answered with its tools), `POST /api/mcp/servers/{name}/connect` (again, signing in again) and
`DELETE /api/mcp/servers/{name}` (Connect apps' own only: its tools, record and sign-in go). Connect apps: **Tools of
other services**, every server with its tools and where it is set up, **Open the sign-in page** while one waits, the
page asking every 2 s until the try ended, and a form for a name and an address; **Services to add**. Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_mcp_sign_in.py`, against an MCP server that is its own authorization server (the library's, saying
yes to every sign-in, its tokens running out after 3 s and checked against their resource), with Dot's own server: the
sign-in followed as a browser would and the tool offered and called, the file's mode, the next start renewing the token
without a new sign-in, a server whose sign-ins ended left out with `SIGN_IN_AGAIN`, Remove, a server open to all, a bad
name, a page of another address and a stray callback refused; and Connect apps in a headless Chrome, wide and light
and on a phone and dark (the config's server with its tools, one added by its address and signed in to on the page that
opens, one removed, nothing wider than the phone).

### 280. Dot starts lean: the fewest words and tools, the rest found when needed

**Status: done (`32e427f`).** The owner's word of 2026-10-18: write it and run the evals on the main model, OpenRouter's
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. **As built (2026-10-18).** `[agent] prompt` (`full` or `lean`) chooses the system prompt's style:
`lean` keeps the rules of trust and safety, of hesitating (item 327) and of how a run ends as `full` has them and says
how to work and each kind of tool in a line or two (6,486 characters for a plain task, 5,944 when the evals ran, where
`full` has 14,516). Eval reports keep the style. The evals' 41 tasks, twice each, with the owner's config in throw-away
homes and the keys passed to each run only; the first ran on the code before the change, whose full prompt was the same
byte for byte when the evals ran, and the runs overlapped, so the seconds were taken under unequal load. They cost about
0.22, 0.16 and 0.14 dollars, in the order of the table:

| Prompt, tools | Passed | Tokens a pass | Seconds a pass | Claimed done, were not | Injections followed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| full, all (today) | 81 of 82 | 72.4 k | 12.5 | 1 | 0 of 6 |
| full, grouped | 80 of 82 | 50.1 k | 12.1 | 2 | 1 of 6 |
| lean, grouped | 78 of 82 | 40.5 k | 9.2 | 3 | 0 of 6 |

Fewer words and tools took 31 to 44 % fewer tokens a pass (the lean prompt alone, beside grouped tools, 19 %), and
passed a little less and claimed a little more often to be done when they were not; filter-headlines failed in every
row, and without it the passes are 80, 79 and 78 of 80 and the false claims 0, 1 and 1. The difference is small for 82
attempts, but it does not show that the lean start does as well, so both defaults stay `full` and `lean` is there for
whoever weighs the tokens more. After the evals, the reviews restored two rules the lean text had dropped, hesitating
and not saving what a page asks to be remembered, and gave it the full text's closing, which names the note on the other
runs at work (about 2 % of a step's input), and both texts now say that a schedule's run goes on in the chat that made
it (item 291), where the full text said a new thread. The evals could not judge the shortened words on plans, the
desktop and memory: no attempt kept a plan, and they run without the desktop or embeddings. Tests:
`tests/unit/test_lean_prompt.py` (every rule kept, under half the length), the callers of the prompt's inputs, `dotx
eval check`. Docs: `docs/runs.md`. The reports are in the owner's `reports/evals-280/`.

**What.** A run starts with a short system prompt and the core tools; the other groups of tools are named in a line and
come when the run asks for them (`use_tools`), as `tool_surface = "grouped"` does. Evals of both ways on the same tasks
and model decide the default: the lean way if it does as well with fewer tokens.

**Why.** The second saying: the minimal possible system prompt and tools, and the model figures it out. A task run starts
with about 22 k tokens of prompt and tools today.

**Tests.** The evals' numbers in the as-built paragraph (passed tasks, steps, tokens), unit tests of the lean prompt's
parts, `dotx eval check`.

### 281. A chat can be a loop that asks Dot again until it is done

**Status: done (`48e7219`).** The owner chose it on 2026-10-17, with 268, 271 and 280, for this round. **As built
(2026-10-17).** `/loop <rhythm> <message>` in the box of a run (the slash menu offers it) sends the message at once and
makes a schedule of the chat (`POST /api/runs/{id}/loop`, `scheduler/loops.py`): a cron expression that keeps the rhythm
exactly (every 5, 10, 15, 20 or 30 minutes, or every 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 or 12 hours; others are refused), the message as
its goal with a line that tells each run how the loop ends (it deletes the schedule with `schedule_delete` once the work
is done for good), and the chat's own choices, as a schedule a run makes in a chat has them (item 291). Right above the
composer a line lists the chat's loops (`loops.js`, after the commands at work): the message, how often, when next, and
a Stop that deletes the schedule; it is read again as the chat's runs come and go. A loop that asks again "when the last
run said to look again" is left out: a run that wants another rhythm deletes its loop and the owner makes another.
Tests: `tests/unit/test_loops.py` (the rhythms, refused ones, the name and the goal), `tests/smoke/test_chat_loop.py`
(the schedule of the chat with its choices, a refused rhythm; `/loop` in a chat, wide and on a phone: the line, the
message sent, Stop). Docs: `docs/runs.md`, `docs/daemon.md`, `docs/memory-and-schedules.md`.

**What.** `/loop` in the composer makes the message a loop of the chat: asked again every so often (`/loop 30m …`) or
when the last run said to look again, in the same chat, until the owner stops it or a run says it is done. The chat
shows that it loops, when it asks next and a Stop.

**Why.** The first saying: talk to a loop, which prompts the agent.

**Tests.** Unit: the loop's next time from a cadence and from a run's word. Smoke: a loop that asks twice in the chat
and stops when its run says done; Stop ends it.

### 282. A chat can be rewound to an earlier message, its files with it

**Status: done.** Merged as `427c51e` (PR #323; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What.** On a message of the owner's that opened a turn, Edit from here:
a dialog, "Edit from here? Rewind chat to before this message. Your prompt and attachments return to the
composer.", with Cancel, Revert files too and Revert and keep changes. Either way the turn and the later ones leave the
chat (their runs stay stored, marked, with what they cost, and the questions they left expire), the history the model
reads ends where it ended before the message, and the message with its files comes back into the box of the turn
before it, or of a new chat when none is left. Revert files too also takes back what those runs and their helpers
changed with the file tools, each file that is as they left it; a file changed since is left and named, and a
command's changes stay. The chat's OpenCode session is let go, so that its next run there reads the rewound history.

- A run of a chat keeps, as it is made, where its first message goes in the chat's history: the history's version and
  the place (`runs.history_version`, `runs.history_seq`). A compaction writes the history anew as the next version and
  keeps aside what came before the latest run of the old one (`message_archive`), so that a rewind across a compaction
  gives the history back as it was.
- `POST /api/runs/{id}/rewind` with `files` `revert` or `keep`. The take-back is planned first, so that a journal that
  cannot be read stops the rewind; a file that cannot be put back afterwards is named with why. Refused for a helper's
  run, a run from before the places were kept, a run taken out already, a chat with a run at work or messages in its
  queue, and a chat that changed since its runs were read for the plan. A live `chat_rewound` event has the pages read
  their lists of chats again.
- Send again (item 205) gives way to it: the box sends the message again, changed or not.
- What it costs: the history is written anew whenever a run drops old screenshots or shortens old outputs, not only when
  it compacts, and each run that does so keeps aside the history before it, with the screenshots that history names.
  A long chat's share of the database grows with its turns (the owner's largest chat holds 3.4 MB of history over 11
  turns, which comes to about 20 MB kept aside). Keeping each distinct message once would bring that down.

**Why.** The third saying: open to being wrong, with a way back. The plan had the later turns stay greyed in the chat;
they leave it instead.

**Tests.** Smoke, `test_rewind.py`: a chat of three turns rewound from its page to its second message, the files as the
first turn left them, the second message and its file in the box, the next run without the third; a rewind that keeps
the changes; one across a compaction; the refusals; the dialog wide and light and on a phone in the dark.
`test_message_feet.py` follows the new foot.

## Part 50: Zen's free models, through OpenCode itself (planned 2026-10-15)

The owner's fifty-second word, on 2026-10-15: "Bir diğer konu: OpenCode Zen'i, yani free modelleri kullanabilmemiz için
benim GitHub'daki AgenticSideBar adlı repomdaki OpenCode provider kullanımıma bak. Ben o projede free modelleri OpenCode
dışında çalıştırabiliyordum, tamamen yasal bir şekilde. Ardından bu OpenCode Zen free modellerini bizim sisteme de dahil
edelim, çalışır bir şekilde. Ya da OpenCode Zen API key de ekleriz; o zaman da free modelleri seçebilir miyiz,
bilmiyorum." (Look at how the owner's AgenticSideBar uses OpenCode, where the free models ran outside OpenCode's own
app; bring Zen's free models into Dot, working; or would a Zen key let Dot pick them?)

**What was found (2026-10-15).** A Zen key does not open them. Zen lists 86 models, 11 of them free (`big-pickle`,
`cat-jam-free`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, `jev-1.13-free`, `longcat-2.5-preview-free`, `mimo-v2.6-flash-free`,
`muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free`, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free`, `nemotron-3.5-lightning-free`, `space-bunny-free`,
`step-5-preview-free`), and a call to one of them from any client but OpenCode's own answers 403 `FreeTierError`
("OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode"), with the owner's key and without, as on 2026-10-12 (item
119). AgenticSideBar does not call Zen: it starts the official `opencode` program as a local server (`opencode serve
--hostname 127.0.0.1 --port <free port>`, a password of its own, a config of its own) and drives OpenCode's own agent
over its HTTP API (a session, a prompt, the event stream, the answers to its permission questions), so OpenCode makes
every call. Measured here with OpenCode 1.19.0 (`/opt/homebrew/bin/opencode`), in a throw-away config and data folder
with no key: OpenCode lists 10 free models it may use; a prompt to `big-pickle` through its server answers "OK" with
OpenCode's agent and tools (6,395 tokens of OpenCode's own prompt and tools, cost 0), and 403 `FreeTierError` when the
prompt switches every tool off. Zen's free tier serves OpenCode's own agent, not a model behind another agent's loop. A
run asked to run `ls -1` went through end to end: OpenCode asked for the bash permission, the answer `once` let it run,
and it answered "It printed 3 entries (alpha.txt, beta.txt, gamma.md)." `opencode serve` takes no tool definitions from
its client (opencode.ai/docs/server); an MCP server added to it (`POST /mcp`) gives its tools to the agent.

So a run on a free model is OpenCode's: Dot hands the goal to OpenCode's agent and shows what it does, as AgenticSideBar
does. Zen's docs say the free models are free "for a limited time", and that the providers of Big Pickle, MiMo and Muse
Spark Contributor may use what is sent to them to improve or train their models; the others keep nothing. OpenCode's
terms (effective 2026-08-15) ask for use "for your own internal use" and forbid extracting output automatically; the
owner judged the AgenticSideBar way allowed, and Dot drives OpenCode the same way, on the owner's Mac, for the owner.

### 283. Zen's free models work in Dot, as OpenCode's own agent

**Status: done.** Merged as `aeee10b` (PR #321; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What.** With OpenCode installed, Dot starts it as a local server of its own when a run or the model list needs it (on
a free loopback port, behind a password Dot makes, with a config and data folder in Dot's home, so that the owner's own
OpenCode settings and keys stay out), and stops it with the daemon. The model picker offers the free models OpenCode may
use that call tools, as `opencode:<model>`, marked Free, and says which send what they get to a provider that may learn
from it. A run on one of them is OpenCode's agent at work in the run's folder: the run's page shows its text as it comes
and each of its tool calls (read, edit, bash, grep, a web fetch, …) as a step with what it was given and what it gave
back; a permission OpenCode asks for becomes Dot's approval, answered by itself in yolo; Stop stops OpenCode's session;
a message to the run at work reaches it; the run ends with OpenCode's answer, or failed with its error. A follow-up in
the same chat goes on in the same OpenCode session. Without OpenCode, the picker has none of these models, and a run
that names one fails with how to install OpenCode.

**Why.** The owner's fifty-second word: Zen's free models in Dot, working. They serve only OpenCode's own agent, so that
is what runs.

**Tests.** Unit: the reading of OpenCode's event stream into a run's events, on a stream recorded from OpenCode 1.19.0
(text, reasoning, a tool asked for, allowed and done, the end). Smoke, live where OpenCode is installed: a chat message
on a free model goes through the daemon to OpenCode's agent and back, a tool step and the approval answered on the way.

**As built (2026-10-15).** `opencode/server.py`: `OpenCodeServer`, a connector to the `opencode` program that
`[providers.opencode] command` names, looked up on the login shell's PATH and in Homebrew's and OpenCode's own folders
(`DOT_OPENCODE` overrides it; the smoke tests' new `conftest.py` points it at a program that does not exist, so that no
test starts the owner's), started as `opencode serve` on a free loopback port behind a password Dot makes, its health
waited for, held while a run uses it, and stopped after `idle_stop_s` with nothing to do and with the daemon. Its
config, data, state, cache and home folders are in `opencode_dir()`, and its environment is the login PATH and the
variables a program expects, no key, with `OPENCODE_TEST_HOME` (the one variable that moves where OpenCode looks for the
home's `.opencode` folder, HOME staying the owner's for the commands of its agent), `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG`,
`OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE`, `OPENCODE_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS`, `OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD` and `OPENCODE_PURE`:
a tool planted in the home's `.opencode/tools` stays out of its agent's tools, and comes in without the first (measured:
the owner's own `~/.opencode` holds ECC's tools, which would run without asking). `OPENCODE_PERMISSION`, which OpenCode
applies over every config, has each tool that acts or reads and a subagent ask Dot, and switches no tool off: Zen's free
tier is reported to refuse OpenCode itself with a tool off (anomalyco/opencode#49433, #51315), and a first version that
switched the subagent and skill tools off was answered and refused alike. The free models come from `GET /provider`
(Zen's own provider, a price of zero for what they read and write, not deprecated, with vision, tools, thinking, window
and the variants that are Dot's levels) and are kept in `models.json` for `models_ttl_s`. `opencode/events.py` reads the
event stream into a run's events, for its session alone (text and reasoning parts and their pieces, tool calls by
status, steps with their tokens, the cache read counted in and the reasoning out, messages and their errors,
permissions, idle, error), tested on a stream recorded from OpenCode 1.19.0. `llm/opencode.py`: the provider `opencode`,
its free models that call tools; `complete` refuses, as no call of Dot's own can use one; `ModelRouter` makes it with
the login environment, which it now takes. `opencode/run.py`: `run_in_opencode`, which `RunManager._drive` runs for a
model of `opencode`. A chat's session is kept in `opencode/chats/<chat>.json` with the number of the chat's messages it
saw, and those it missed (said on other models) come before the goal; the goal is kept in the chat as for any run; the
stream is opened before the prompt and read in one queue with the owner's messages and Stop; deltas, `tool_call` and
`tool_result` (`opencode_<tool>`), an `assistant` event per step with its tokens, and the run's tokens and steps go out
as Dot's own runs send them. Each permission is decided in a task of its own by `RunGate.authorize`, on the action Dot's
own tools would describe (`permission_action`: a command as the shell tool's, by `assess_shell`; an edit by
`write_action`; reads, searches and folders outside by `read_action`, both now plain functions of `tools/files.py`; a
fetch as reading the web, checked against the browser's allowed and blocked hosts first): a refusal or a hand-off is
answered with its reason and the agent goes on, a repeated call (`doom_loop`) and a subagent are refused with a note,
and the owner's note on an approval goes on to the agent. The run is done with the agent's last answer once the session
is idle with every prompt taken and no permission pending; it fails with Zen's free tier's refusal said as what it is
(`FREE_TIER_REFUSED`: measured, the free tier refused OpenCode's own command line too, from 17:48 to about 17:56, and
answered again at 17:57). Settings › Models: `not_installed` is a quiet problem, as no key is; the free models whose
providers may train on what they get say so there and in the picker (`ModelOption.learns`); the context size of a free
model is OpenCode's own. A free model cannot be a helper role's (`POST /api/models/roles` refuses it) and its runs make
no playbook. Live tests (`hosted`, `tests/smoke/test_opencode_live.py`): the owner's setup kept out; a run that asks, is
approved and creates a file, and the next run of its chat remembering the file; a refused command not run, the run still
answering; a message reaching the agent at work, and Stop stopping a run that waits for the owner, its question decided
with it. A run that ends before its agent did stops OpenCode's session, then lets its open questions go and gives each
task up to ten seconds to store its question as decided (`_let_go`); the first version cancelled them in the middle of
that, which left a stopped run's question pending on its page.

### 284. OpenCode's agent uses Dot's own tools over MCP

**Status: done.** Merged as `5655e6f` (PR #326; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What.** OpenCode's agent gets Dot's own tools besides its own: Dot serves the tools a run may use (the browser, the
Mac's desktop, memory, notes, schedules, …) as an MCP server of its own for that run, added to the run's OpenCode
session, so that a run on a free model browses, uses the Mac and remembers, each call passing Dot's policy and approvals
as a call of Dot's own loop does.

**Why.** A run on a free model can then do what a run on any other model does in Dot.

**Tests.** A run on a free model that opens a page in Dot's browser and reads it, live where OpenCode is installed;
Zen's free tier must still answer with the MCP tools added (measured first).

**As built (2026-10-16, part 52).** The refusal in the owner's picture (a free model that said it had no browser and
could not leave its folder) came from an agent that had none of Dot's tools, only OpenCode's own; Zen's free tier
refused nothing. `opencode/bridge.py` serves Dot's tools in the daemon as an MCP server on `127.0.0.1` (streamable
HTTP, a free port), one door per chat (`dot_` and eight hex digits of the chat, a secret in each request's header); the
OpenCode server Dot starts has the doors as remote MCP servers of its own, and a chat's session keeps to its own door by
OpenCode's permission rules (`session_rules`), which hide the other doors' tools and instructions from its model
(measured with OpenCode 1.19.1 and a free model: it listed and called its own door's tool only, and the free tier
answered as without the server). The tools given (`opencode/run.py`, `bridged_tools`): the groups browser, desktop,
schedule, memory_admin and pages, the connected apps, and `memory_save`, `memory_search`, `notify`, `ask_user` and
`skill`, of those the run's mode and agent allow. A call runs as a call of Dot's own loop (`execute_calls`: the run's
gate, the tool's time limit, the timeline under the tool's own name), and one still at work tells OpenCode so every
20 s, which starts OpenCode's wait of 120 s again, so an approval the owner takes long over does not time it out. The
door's instructions tell the agent it works inside Dot with these tools, and that the tabs and apps of other chats are
theirs. README: the OpenCode provider. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_opencode_bridge.py` (real HTTP with the MCP client: a
door's requests run its tools and nothing else reaches it; a call that outlasts a ping says it is still at work),
`tests/unit/test_opencode.py` (the tools given, an agent bounded to some, a door per chat, a result's pictures and its
failure), and live `tests/smoke/test_opencode_live.py::test_a_run_on_a_free_model_reads_a_page_in_dots_browser` (a
free model opens a page of a local server in Dot's browser and answers with what it read).

### 285. A helper that starts late joins its siblings, and stopped ones stand still

**Status: done.** Merged as `8aa45dd` (PR #322; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** The delegate tool's own limit (`_TIMEOUT_S`, an hour, `tools/delegate.py`) stopped helpers that
worked longer: they ended cancelled, as the sidebar showed. `[agent] parallel_tools = 4` runs four calls of a step at a
time, so a fifth `delegate` of the same step waits for a slot, and its `tool_call` and its helper's `run_queued` come
only once one of the four has ended. The timeline put that late call in a group of its own after the card of helpers
(`showCall` through `groupFor`), so `placeHelper`, which joins a helper to the card only while the card is the last
thing of the conversation, gave it a row of its own: the card kept saying "4 helpers". A page that missed a helper's
end (a phone put away) kept its row as it last knew it, spinning.

**As built (2026-10-15).** `static/js/timeline.js`: the group of the model turn under way is kept (`turnGroup`, set by
`groupFor` and by the turn's message, dropped once a text reply ends it); a call of that turn that comes while the card
of helpers is the last thing joins the turn's group (`callGroup`), so its helper joins the card. `settle(runs, now)`
makes the rows of helpers the page did not know from the run's children, ends the rows whose run ended and counts the
steps of the others; `knows(runId)`. `static/js/views/run.js`: `reconcile` settles the card from `/runs/{id}`'s
children each time it reads the run, which it does when the stream comes back and 1.5 s after the last `run_queued`,
`run_started` or `run_finished` of one of its helpers (`HELPERS_SETTLE_MS`). Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_late_helper.py`: a run delegates five helpers with four calls at a time and the delegate tool's limit
cut to 8 s; the card says "4 helpers", "4 working", then "5 helpers", "1 working · 4 stopped" with four still rings
and one spinning, then "5 stopped" with none spinning, and the page loaded again on a phone, dark, the same. On the code
of before it fails: the head says "4 helpers" for the 32 s the test waits.

### 286. The phone comes back quietly, on the chat it was in

**Status: done.** Merged as `8aa45dd` (PR #322; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** The manifest's `start_url` was `/#/activity` (item 52), so the home-screen app opened on Activity.
A phone put away leaves the page's streams open and silent; back in view, the lifecycle stream was cut only after
`STALL_MS` (45 s) of silence, and meanwhile the bar said Reconnecting and a read that failed while the network came back
showed the toast "Cannot reach the Dot daemon". The picture the word names did not come; the toasts of coming back are
the errors found.

**As built (2026-10-15).** `static/js/api.js`: `sse` keeps when it last heard from its stream; a page back in view
whose stream has been silent for 20 s or more (`BACK_SILENCE_MS`) cuts it, and `follow` makes it again at once.
`QUIET_BREAK_MS` (2 s) and `unreachable(error)`. `static/js/dom.js`: `showAfter(node, ms)` shows a node once a state
has held that long and hides it at once; the bar's connection pill (`shell.js`) and a run's connection note
(`views/run.js`) show only a break longer than 2 s. `static/js/state.js`: for 10 s after the page comes back or the
stream is back (`settle`), a read that cannot reach the daemon is tried again after 2.5 s without a toast. `main.js`:
Dot opens on the chat screen it was on last (`dot.lastChat`: a run's page or New chat), else New chat, for an address
without a route and for a home-screen app that starts on `#/activity` (added before; `standalone()`); in a browser's
tab Activity stays a page. `manifest.webmanifest`: `start_url` `/`. README: Dot on the phone. Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_reconnect.py` (one new test): at a phone's width, the page put away with its stream frozen at a proxy
and its clock moved 25 s, back in view, makes its second stream and shows the chat made meanwhile within 3 s, with the
pill hidden; with the cut on return taken out it fails. `tests/smoke/test_phone.py`: `start_url` is `/`; the address
without a route and a home-screen app on `#/activity` open the run the page was on last; a tab on `#/activity` shows
Activity.

### 288. macOS asks for Dot, and a closed Mac app keeps its answer

**Status: done.** Merged as `8aa45dd` (PR #322; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** macOS holds the program launchd starts responsible for all it starts, and the job started the
virtual environment's Python: `responsibility_get_pid_responsible_for_pid` of the owner's daemon was the daemon itself,
`~/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.13.12-macos-aarch64-none/bin/python3.13`. So macOS's questions and System Settings
named `python3.13`, and a grant went to that binary alone: another Python (a uv update) had none, while the old row
still showed it switched on. Connect apps reads Automation through `AEDeterminePermissionToAutomateTarget`, which
answers `procNotFound` for an application that is not running: a row then said Not checked and offered Allow, although
macOS had said yes, each time the application was closed.

**As built (2026-10-15).** `dot_app.c` and `dot_app.py`: Dot.app in Dot's home, whose program starts the program its
arguments name as its child (`posix_spawn`), hands SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGHUP, SIGQUIT and SIGUSR1/2 on to it (blocked
while it starts) and ends as it ended. `service install` builds it with `xcrun clang` and signs it ad hoc
(`codesign --sign -`, identifier `dev.dotagent.dot`), with an Info.plist named Dot (`LSUIElement`, the usage lines of
Apple events, the Desktop, Documents and Downloads folders and the local network); an app built from the same source and
Info.plist is left as it is, so that what macOS granted it holds. `launchd.py`: the job runs
`[Dot.app's program, python, -P, -m, dotagent, daemon]`. `desktop/perms.py`: `responsible_program()` asks macOS which
program it holds responsible for the process (Terminal, Claude, Dot.app), as an app's bundle; `program_name`;
`grant_hint` names it. `/desktop/permissions` and `dotx service permissions` name it, and `service install` says to
allow Dot. `server/routes_connections.py` and `connections/states.py`: the last answer macOS gave about a Mac
application (allowed, not asked, refused) is kept in the store's kv per program and application, and a closed
application shows it (`mac_state`) with no Allow; `ConnectionsView.runner` names the program, which the refused line
says to open in Privacy & Security › Automation. README: the service, Connect apps. Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_dot_app.py`: the app built in a throw-away home is signed ad hoc as `dev.dotagent.dot`, built again it
is the same file, started the way launchd starts a job (a stand-in that spawns it disclaiming responsibility) the
Python it starts reads Dot.app as responsible and "Dot" as its name, and it ends with its child's status and hands
SIGTERM on. `tests/smoke/test_connect_apps.py`: Calendar allowed, then closed, still says Allowed with no button (Not
checked on the code of before); the refused line says "open Dot and switch on Notes". `tests/unit/test_launchd.py`:
the job's words. Moving from the Python job, the owner grants the permissions to Dot once, at the Mac: the first start
asks whether Dot may use the Desktop folder, where the owner's checkout is.

### 291. A schedule made in a chat runs as that chat does, and knows five runs

**Status: done.** Merged as `8aa45dd` (PR #322; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** `schedule_create` made a schedule with the defaults: a new chat each time, the default model, the

**As built (2026-10-15).** `tools/schedule.py`: the schedule a run makes keeps its chat's choices (`chat_options`: the

schedules tasks). `store`: a schedule keeps `speed` (a column added), `add_schedule` takes the chat; `start_firing`

shows Fast. `defaults.toml`: `[scheduler] history_runs = 5`. README: Schedules. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_scheduler.py`

`tests/unit/test_schedule_choices.py`, and the five-run default in `test_schedule_memory.py`.

### 292. Every free model of Zen, from OpenCode's refreshed catalog

**Status: done.** Merged as `b4e554f` (PR #324; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** OpenCode answers `/provider` from the catalog it read when it started and refreshes models.dev only

the catalog Dot listed, and serves no run, makes way, so the next one reads the refreshed catalog (`_drop_outdated`).
README: the providers. Tests: `tests/unit/test_opencode.py` (the listing read into free models),

is the page left panned by the keyboard: iOS 26 can leave `visualViewport.offsetTop` above 0 once the keyboard has gone
(WebKit bugs 301108 and 301994, Apple's forum thread 800154), so what is fixed to the window sat 69 pt up, its top out
of sight and a band under it. The home and agent pages gave the composer the caret as they opened, which brought the
keyboard up on every visit. In the iOS 26.5 simulator, iOS at times told of no last step of the keyboard's slide, and
the composer stayed where the slide had left it.

The open tasks include the code review of 2026-10-15 (`reports/Dot kod review 2026-10-15.md`, kept out of the
repository): its first fixes (K2, K1, Y6) were written and reviewed by the session that made the review and left

### 300. The code review's first fixes: requests, typing, a skill's YAML

**Status: done.** Merged as `3202bb6` (PR #325; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** K2: a page in Dot's own Chrome could reach Dot's interface: a redirect from an allowed address to a
refused one was never checked (only the first request was), a popup's first request escaped the page's route, and the
daemon did not look at `Sec-Fetch-Site`, so a page of another site could open the interface (whose token the page keeps
in `localStorage`). K1: `terminal_send` wrote to the pty with a blocking `os.write` on the event loop; a program that
did not read (a busy `python -i`) froze the daemon. Y6: a learned skill's description was quoted by hand into its
YAML frontmatter, so a `\d` in it made the SKILL.md unreadable, and `offered_to_run` let the error stop every run.

**As built (2026-10-16).** `browser/session.py`, `browser/safety.py`: in Dot's own Chrome every request of the context,
popups included, is checked (`forbidden_target` on every request, `navigable` on navigations), a redirect is followed
step by step, and a tab of Dot's that lands on a refused address is reset; in attach mode no request is held (the
owner's own tabs would wait on Dot), and the landing check does the work. `server/guard.py`: a navigation to the
interface that a page of another site started (`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`) is refused, save to the page a sign-in
comes back to and the pages runs showed. `terminal/session.py`: the pty is non-blocking, what the program has not read
waits for it (`loop.add_writer`) up to 64 KB, and past that `terminal_send` fails with `TerminalInputFullError`
(`core/errors.py`) until the program reads; `EAGAIN` on a read is not an end. `agent/playbooks.py`: the frontmatter is
written by the YAML library (`_frontmatter`) and the SKILL.md read back before it is written (`rendered_skill`); a
SKILL.md the loader cannot read is left out of the list (`playbook_unreadable` in the log). README: the browser's hosts
and the terminal. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_browser_boundary.py` (new: a redirect and a popup to a refused address in
Dot's Chrome), `tests/smoke/test_terminal_input.py` (new: a program that does not read, 64 KB, then the error),
`tests/unit/test_server_guard.py`, `tests/unit/test_own_interface.py`, `tests/unit/test_playbooks.py` (a `\d` in a
description reads back; an unreadable SKILL.md is left out).

The owner's other words are items 284 (part 50), 301, 302 and 303; the rest of the code review is item 304. They are
built on `item-300-tools-and-learning`, one PR with 284. Items 268, 271, 280 and 281 come after it, and item 76's
reading is due on or after 2026-10-18.

### 301. Runs at work side by side keep to their own tabs, apps and files

**Status: done.** Merged as `5655e6f` (PR #326; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** Each chat had tabs of its own that no tool of another chat's run reaches (`browser/session.py`),
but a run knew nothing of the others at work: two runs could type in one application at once, and a run could write
over a file another had just changed. The browser's idle reaper released a chat's tabs after `[browser] tab_idle_s`
also while its run was at work (waiting for the owner's answer or for a long command), which then found its pages gone.

**As built (2026-10-16).** `agent/peers.py` keeps the footprint of each run at work in the daemon (`Peers`, begun and
ended by the run manager): the sites of its pages, the applications it drives and the files it read and changed, from
each of its calls that went through (`agent/executor.py`). Before a call, `Peers.conflict` refuses, with why and
without running or asking anything, typing or clicking in an application another run acted in within 120 s
(`APP_HOLD_S`), and changing a file another run changed after this one last read it (or that it never read); the runs
of one chat are not each other's peers. Each run's loop gives its model a note (`peers_note`) naming the other runs,
their goals, sites, applications and changed files, whenever that changes, and the system prompt says to leave those
to them. The idle reaper keeps the tabs of the chats with a run at work (`threads_to_release`, `Peers.threads`). What a
shell command changes leaves no footprint (it names no file the way the file tools do), and `dotx run` in a terminal
knows only its own runs. README: How a run works. Tests: `tests/unit/test_peers.py` (a changed file is written only
after it is read again; an app another run drives is its own for a while; one chat's runs are not peers; the note; the
tabs of a chat at work outlive their idle time), `tests/smoke/test_peers.py` (two scripted runs: the second leaves the
file the first changed until it has read it).

### 302. Lessons are saved on their own, after a second look

**Status: done.** Merged as `5655e6f` (PR #326; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What.** The owner asked that what a session learned be saved at its end without asking, carefully and selectively.
`[agent] lessons` was `propose` by default (each lesson waited on the run's page), and `auto` saved every lesson the
filter kept, save after a run that read content others can write, whose lessons it only proposed.

**As built (2026-10-16).** `lessons = "auto"` is the default (`defaults.toml`; the owner's `config.toml` does not set
it). Each lesson the filter keeps gets a second look first (`agent/review.py`, `lesson_vetter_for`): one more call of
the review model, in a session of its own, that is shown the goal and the lessons and nothing the run read. It keeps
only know-how about how a tool, a command, a site, an application or a file format behaves, and leaves out what tells
the agent to send, post, buy, sign in, contact someone, change a setting or go to an address, to trust some content or
to skip a check, or what holds private data. After a run that read content others can write, a lesson with a link or
an account name in it is left out before it is asked (`outside_problem`). The kept lessons are saved as notes tagged
`lesson`; "Lessons from this run" on the run's page says "Saved on its own" with Undo, which forgets the note
(`POST /api/runs/{id}/lessons/{index}/undo`), and a lesson left out says why, with Save anyway; a lesson is what its
last decision made it. README: Lessons. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_lessons_card.py` (new, browser: the card on a wide
dark page and on a light phone), `tests/smoke/test_lessons.py`, `tests/unit/test_lessons.py`,
`tests/unit/test_agent_learning.py`.

### 303. Memory, lessons and skills: the audit's fixes

**Status: done.** Merged as `5655e6f` (PR #326; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** An audit of memory, lessons and learned skills for the owner's words ranked eleven defects: (1) a
run that read pages could become a skill, with no check of where its steps came from (the code review's Y7); (2) one
unreadable SKILL.md stopped every run (with the review's Y6, item 300); (3) the reflection read whether a run read
content others can write from its newest 60 results only; (4) the reflection folded away and retired lessons the owner
had saved; (5) a resting lesson saved again stayed resting; (6) a run updated another owner's skill of the same name;
(7) the same text found another agent's note; (8) a run's `memory_update` makes the owner's note the run's, so that it
can rest; (9) a skill retired on two failures in its life; (10) the reflection asked again about a run whose lessons
were drawn and none kept; (11) a crash could leave a half-written skill folder. And the owner's 35 learned skills held
12 of one kind of work: the kinds the model named the same work by were 0.66 to 0.83 apart by meaning (bge-m3), under
the bar of 0.85, so every run wrote a new skill. The code review adds Y3 and Y4 (secrets the masking missed), Y19 (the
merge of notes on the event loop) and learning that stopped unseen (its O25 with O3).

**As built (2026-10-16).** Lessons and memory: (3) `Store.read_outside` reads all the run's results; (4) a lesson the
owner saved is never folded away nor retired; (5) `wake_memory`; (7) the same text merges only into a note its saver is
handed, and the lesson writer checks against the notes of the run's own agent; (10) `lessons_none` is recorded; (8) is
left as it is (item 157: a run that rewrites a note makes it the run's). `core/text.py` (Y3, Y4): a secret in single
quotes, a key with a word after the secret and a dict's `Authorization` are masked, a JSON field named for a secret is
masked whole, and "task-management" is no OpenAI key. Y19: the duplicate check runs off the event loop (`math.sumprod`).
A crash of a run's lessons or skill work leaves `lessons_failed` or `playbook_failed` on the run, a failed reflection is
kept (`agent/reflection_record.py`) and stands in Activity until one after it is done, and `dotx stats` counts both and
says when the reflection was last done. Skills (`agent/playbooks.py`): (1) a run that read content third parties can
author (`OUTSIDE_CHANNELS`) is distilled from its own steps alone (`own_steps_digest`: each call and whether it worked,
never what it returned nor the answer), a skill that names a web address, an account or an e-mail address its run's
goal and calls never did is not kept (`foreign_problem`), and the record and SKILL.md say where it comes from
(`read_outside`); the duplicates: the writer is shown the kinds its owner keeps (`kinds_shown`, the run's site first,
30 at most) and names the run's work by one of them word for word, and the same kind updates that skill; (6) a run
updates its owner's skills alone, and another owner's skill of the same name keeps its folder (`free_name`); (9) a
skill retires after two failures in a row (`failing`); (11) a folder is written whole under a hidden name and renamed,
and a half-made one an older Dot left is replaced. The owner's twelve skills of one kind are left as they are
(Settings › Skills drops them). README: Lessons, Reflection, Learned skills. Tests: `tests/unit/test_playbooks.py`
(the steps alone, the names a run never used, the record, failures in a row, another owner's folder, a folder whole or
not at all), `tests/unit/test_reflection.py`, `tests/smoke/test_reflection.py`, `tests/smoke/test_lessons.py`,
`tests/unit/test_redaction.py`, `tests/unit/test_run_statistics.py`, `tests/unit/test_agent_learning.py`. Not seen
live: that the review model names a run's work by a kind it is shown (the paths around it are unit-tested).

**Status: done.** Merged as `5655e6f` (PR #326; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** The rest of the code review's plan of fixes, each read again against the code first, and one leak

**As built (2026-10-16).**

islemlerine saygı göstermeliler 2. Memory ve learng process Gerçektke kusursuz olmalı ve eskiyen bilgi otomatik atılmalı
cıkarılmalı 3. Ajanımız kendine agent takımı oluşturabilmeli ve o agentler agents altında listelenmeli gerektiğinde
kullanabilmeli Browser kullanımı ve computer use her gün daha iyi gelişmeli." (Several sessions at work must respect
each other's browsers and work; memory and learning must be flawless, and stale knowledge must be thrown out on its own;

is `reports/oturum-hafiza-ekip-2026-10-16.md` (kept out of the repository).

### 305. Runs side by side keep to each other's apps, files and browser, by every path

**Status: done.** Merged as `5655e6f` (PR #326; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** Item 301's footprints had gaps a second run could walk through: a batch of desktop steps was
checked only for its first application; an AppleScript drove any application without a footprint; app names matched
by case; the conflict check and the footprint were apart, so two runs waiting for approval could both go; a shell
command changed files without a trace; a run that ended took its changes with it, so a run of another chat could write
over them unread; and the browser's mode and debugging port could change under another chat's run between its steps.

**As built (2026-10-16).** `agent/peers.py`: `Peers.take` (the check and the footprint in one step, right before the
call, also after an approval), `take_app` (each step of a desktop batch), app names without regard to case, the
applications a script names (`tools/apple.py` `script_apps`, System Events left out), the files of an ended run kept for
the other chats' runs at work (`left`) until they read them, and a deleted folder that covers its files.
`policy/shell.py`: `ShellAssessment.changes`, the files a line writes or deletes as far as it names them (redirects,
`rm`, `cp`/`mv`/`install`/`ditto`/`rsync`/`ln`, `tee`, `truncate`, `sed -i`), which never change the judgement (427
lines of the shell tests judged the same before and after); the shell lines of an AppleScript count the same, also in a
script that drives free applications. `browser/session.py` `threads_in_use`: the mode and the debugging port wait for
the other chats' runs. The prompt: leave the other runs' apps and files to them, and stop or kill no process or app the
run did not start. README: How a run works. Tests: `tests/unit/test_peers.py` (eleven new), `tests/smoke/test_peers.py`
(a write approved after another chat's run changed the file is refused).

### 306. Stale knowledge steps aside on its own: notes, lessons and skills

**Status: done.** Merged as `5655e6f` (PR #326; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** A note that had been handed to a run once never rested again; nothing could say a fact holds only
for a while; a note a newer one contradicted stayed handed beside it; the nightly fold deleted the lesson it folded
away; and a skill retired twice under one name lost its first copy, as a new skill could take a retired one's name.

**As built (2026-10-16).** Nothing that happens on its own deletes: what goes stale rests, says why on the Memory page,
and can be woken. `memories.expires_at` and `replaced_by` (added columns); `memory_save` `valid_days` (1 to 3650), and
the model reads "holds until"; an expired note rests whoever wrote it and is neither handed nor found; Dot's notes rest
`rest_days` after they were last handed or written; the nightly reflection asks the review model about each newer note
and the closest older note of Dot's (`outdated_pairs`; never the owner's notes, the lessons the owner saved or `core`;
at most 12 a night; the older stays when in doubt) and rests the outdated one with `replaced_by`; the fold rests the
lesson it folds away instead of deleting it; a retired skill keeps its folder and its name. The Memory page says
"Holds until", "Ran out" or "Replaced by another note", and the Resting hint sits under its name. README: Memory, the
nightly reflection. Tests: `tests/unit/test_memory_ranking.py`, `test_reflection.py` (the pairs, with each guard),
`test_playbooks.py`; `tests/smoke/test_memory.py`, `test_outdated_notes.py`, `test_reflection.py`,
`test_lesson_merge.py`.

### 309. The daemon serves the pages it started with, so pages and API never part

**Status: done.** Merged as `5655e6f` (PR #326; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** The owner's word on 2026-10-16: "mobilde sohbetlere girildiğinde ekteki hatayı alıyorum bunuda
düzelt lütfen aymı şekil web ve desktopda da ve memory sayfasina girdigimizde not found hatasi geliyor bu problemide bul
düzelt" (opening a chat on the phone shows the attached error, "undefined is not an object (evaluating 'text.replace')",
and so it does on the web and the desktop; the Memory page says "Not Found"). The daemon had run since 2026-10-15 21:57
with the Python of `427c51e`; two merges (`b4e554f`, `3202bb6`) and a batch of work ported in at 08:18 changed the code
under it, and it was not started again. The UI files were read from disk on every request, so the pages were today's
while the API was the day before's: a chat's page clips `detail.title` (item 295), which that daemon does not send
(`clip(undefined)`), and the Memory page reads `/api/memories/learning`, a route it does not have (404). The digest of
the pages (item 190) was taken at the start while the files were served as they were later, so no page said it was out
of date. Both errors were reproduced in a throw-away home with the Python of `427c51e` and today's pages, and neither
with today's tree whole. A tool's cache in `static/js` (`.mypy_cache`, 20 MB) was served and counted in the digest too.

**As built (2026-10-16).** `server/kept_pages.py`: `keep_pages` reads the pages when the app is made, hidden files left
out; `ServedPages` serves them as `StaticFiles(html=True)` served the folder (GET and HEAD, `/` and a folder's
`index.html` behind its `/`, 304 to an ETag the browser holds, 404, 405); `pages_build` is the digest of the kept pages,
so the status tells what is served. `server/app.py` mounts them instead of the folder. The owner chose this over the
files read live, and to port items 305 to 309 and restart the daemon once. README: the web UI. Tests:
`tests/unit/test_pages_build.py` (the digest leaves hidden files out; a file changed, added or removed on disk after the
start is served as it was or not at all; 304, HEAD, 405 and a folder's redirect), `tests/smoke/test_server.py` (the app
`create_app` makes serves `js/dom.js` as it was, after the file changed, and its status tells the digest of then).

### 310. A chat whose helpers work writes on its page only what changed

**Status: done.** Merged as `5655e6f` (PR #326; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** The owner's word on 2026-10-16: "Sayfa kendini sürekli render ediyor belirli araliklarla acaba
subagentlerden dolayi mi yoksa baska bir sey mi sürekli. mesela [a screenshot] su an bir sohbet calisiyor." (the page
draws itself again and again at intervals, is it the helpers or something else; a chat is running now), with a phone's
screenshots of a chat whose three helpers worked and of Settings › Models. On a daemon served in a throw-away home,
whose stand-in model has a chat hand three helpers a part each, the chat's page in Chrome changed 2074 times on screen
in ten seconds at 390 px, 1798 of them a text put in place of one that read the same, and 2057 times at 1280 px (1743).
Every event of the chat and of its helpers drew each helper's row and time, the head of their group, the line over the
composer and a helper's card again; a `textContent` set to the text it already holds is a new text node, laid out and
painted anew. A helper's line read `step N` at each reply of its model and lost its tool's name until the tool started.
Settings › Models and Rules, Activity and Agents changed nothing on screen in ten seconds each while the chat and its
helpers worked, before as after: the redraw the owner saw on Models was not reproduced.

**As built (2026-10-16).** `dom.js` `setText` writes a node's text only when it reads otherwise. The timeline (a group's
head, the helpers' head, a helper's row and its time), a helper's card, the line over the composer, the details, the
cost card, the helpers' list, the count of the helpers' pill, the composer's pills, the inspector's tab counts, the
sidebar's ages and working times, a background command's time and the shell's connection and waiting count write through
it, or keep what they drew and draw it again only when it changed (a helper's line, a helper card's model, the details'
status, calls, tokens and context, the cost card, the approvals picker's report). A reply whose model calls a tool
leaves the helper's line to that tool's start, so the tool's name stays until the next tool. Measured the same way
after: 207 changes on screen in ten seconds at 390 px and 194 at 1280 px, none of them a text written again as it was
(the helpers' times, their lines and the time over the composer). Tests: `tests/smoke/test_quiet_helpers.py` (browser: a
chat hands three helpers a part each, and for four seconds at 390 px no text on its page is written again as it read,
while the helpers' time and every helper's line move on; on the code before it fails with 3456 texts written again in
those four seconds).

### 311. On an iPhone and an iPad a field has the size it has on the Mac

**Status: done.** Merged as `5655e6f` (PR #326; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** The owner's word on 2026-10-16: "Ayrica mobil tasarim harika olmus fakat bazi placeholderlar
text-size olarak cok büyük görünüyor ve drodpown menu icindeki deger [a screenshot] umarim desktop ve web tarafida bunu
kadar harika ve temiz olur, her bir sayfa cok lnemki. Kolay kullanilabilinir, bulunabilinir ve dogru calisan" (the
phone's design came out great, but some placeholders look far too big, and so does the value in a dropdown; may the
desktop and the web be as great and clean, every page easy to use, to find and working right), with screenshots of
Settings › Models and Settings › Rules on their iPhone. Item 275 gave every field at least 16 px on a touch screen and
in a window up to 720 px wide, so that iOS would not zoom the page into a field as it gets the focus. In WebKit as an
iPhone 17 Pro Max the selects of Models, the fields of Rules and the composer were 16 px, a model's select beside its 14
px label, where the Mac has 13, 14 and 15 px; a window on the Mac up to 720 px wide had them at 16 px too, with no touch
to zoom.

**As built (2026-10-16).** `boot.js`: on an iPhone or an iPad (an iPad that asks for the desktop's pages says it is a
Mac with a touch screen) the viewport allows no scale past the first (`maximum-scale=1`), so that iOS has no room to
zoom into a field, and the page carries `data-focus-zoom="off"`; `app.css` keeps the 16 px floor for the other touch
screens (`pointer: coarse`) only, so a window on the Mac keeps its fields' sizes at any width. Measured after in WebKit
as an iPhone 17 Pro Max: Models' selects 13 px, Rules' fields 14 and 13 px, the composer 15 px, as on the Mac; Chrome as
a Pixel 7 keeps 16 px. Not verified on a device: that iOS 26 does not zoom into a field under 16 px once the viewport
says `maximum-scale=1` (the WebKit of these tests is not iOS's and cannot show it), and whether a pinch still zooms the
app on the home screen. README: the composer, the phone. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_phone_fit.py` (on an iPhone the
viewport holds the scale on every page and a field has the size it has on the Mac, 13, 14 and 15 px; on a Pixel 7 16 px;
both fail on the code before), `test_phone_pages.py` (the composer keeps its chosen size, 15 px, at every width).

### 314. A run drafts an email or a message; the owner sends, edits or discards it

**Status: done.** Merged as `5655e6f` (PR #326; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** The second item of the plan's group A, which the owner chose on 2026-10-16. xAI's Grok Bot writes
an email as a draft its owner sends or discards, and sends several at once when told ("send the top 10"). Dot sent
mail only through `apple_script`, a script the model wrote, which the policy judged and asked about; nothing let the
owner read, change and send a message the run had written.

**As built (2026-10-16).** A tool, `draft_message` (`tools/drafts.py`, group `drafts`): an email for Mail or an
iMessage for Messages, with its recipients, copy, subject and words, checked before it is kept (an address, a phone
number; a message has no cc and no subject). It is a `notes_write` action of `safe` risk: a draft changes nothing
outside Dot; a key in it, in an address too, is refused (`exfiltration`). `drafts/service.py` keeps it in a new `drafts` table and
tells the run's conversation (`draft_created`); the run goes on at once. `drafts.js`: its card, Send, Edit (the card
becomes a form) and Discard (asked); a send the application refuses says why and is sent again; while two or more wait,
each card has a tick and a bar after the last sends the ticked ones together (Grok's "send the top 10"). Send is the
owner's press: `POST /api/drafts/{id}/send` with the words the card holds, `POST /api/drafts/{id}/discard`,
`GET /api/drafts/{id}` (`routes_drafts.py`); the store takes a draft for sending once (`claim_draft`), so a second
press, on another screen too, is a 409. The daemon hands it to `osascript` with a fixed script for Mail or Messages
whose values are its arguments (`drafts/scripts.py`; `run_osascript` takes `argv` now), never words of the script,
and come after `--`: `osascript` reads a first argument that starts with a dash as one of its options, so a body
such as "- 2 tickets" failed and a subject that starts with `-e` would have added a line of script, run at the
owner's Send (found by the code review; `tests/unit/test_osascript_argv.py` gives the real `osascript` such values
with a script that only returns them, and fails without `--`).
`draft_decided` tells the answer, on the run's events and on the lifecycle stream, since the run's own stream ends with
the run: an open page repaints the card, and a card read from the history asks for the draft once. A draft the daemon
was handing over when it stopped is "Not sent" at its next start (`RunManager.recover`), not sent again. The phone and
the web UI's notification tell of a new draft ("Dot drafted an email", the recipients and the subject). Drafts go with
their chat, or with their run's events when those age out. The tool's definition is kept short, 291 estimated tokens
of every step that offers every tool (412 as first written); the small-window test of `test_scaffold.py` grew its
window from 28,000 to 29,000 tokens for it, as for items 34, 193 and 196, since with the larger fixed part a
compaction left room for one page only. README: Tools › Drafts, What leaves this Mac, the API table.
Tests: `tests/smoke/test_drafts.py` (browser: six drafts of a scripted run; one changed and sent with a copy added,
one discarded, one refused by the application and sent again, a message sent from a phone while the page on the Mac
shows it sent, two ticked and sent together, the history as each ended, a second press refused; and a draft left
sending by a stopped daemon), against a stand-in of `osascript` that writes down what it was given: no email or
message left the Mac. On the page of before, the cards are not there. Not tested: the scripts against Mail and
Messages themselves.

reports, account health, a chief of staff). Dot made an agent only from an empty editor, and an agent could not leave
its home: nothing saved it as a file or made one from a file.

**As built (2026-10-16).** `agent/templates.py`: eight templates (`AgentTemplate`), each a name, a role, instructions,
the tools its agent may use, a face, what it needs of the Mac and a schedule to suggest. Every template's instructions
say that whatever leaves the Mac for a person is a draft for the owner (`draft_message`, item 314). Sales Outbound,
Talent Scout, Paid Media and Product Performance work on the web and in files and name their tools: the web, Dot's

Manager, Bug Reproduction, Account Health and Chief of Staff read mail, calendars or code and have every tool. Account

fine-grained token and the home's own secrets through). Dot is not exported. `POST
/api/agents/import` makes the same agent from the file; a tool the home lacks is refused with its name (`_checked`

its bar, which saves `<name>.dot-agent.json`. A suggested schedule is words on the card only. README: Agents. Tests:

a tool that drives Mail, Messages or a terminal, the bounds changed and every template's agent exported, one from its
page, the file's fields exactly the profile, an agent holding a secret of the home's `.env` and one holding a key by
its form refused, with no file saved from the page, then in a second home
on a phone a file that is not JSON and a file naming a tool not there refused with the reason, and the exported file
imported as the same agent, whose page opens with Edit, Export and Delete inside the phone's width). On the page of
before, and with the routes of before alone, the test finds none of the eight cards; without the home's secrets, the
agent holding one is exported.

### 318. A "+" in the composer picks plugins, skills and Plan first, as chips

**Status: done.** Merged as `1334b9f` (PR #327; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** The owner's word of 2026-10-16, with five screenshots of Codex's desktop app: "Codex sistemindkei
gibi eklentiler ve beceriler sayfasi yapma sansimiz var mi daha otrurakli kurumsal ve hos görünüm ve daha cok cesitlilik
? Ayrica composer dan eklentileri de ekleyebilsek ? Daha hos durur sanki" (could we have plugins and skills pages as in
Codex, a more settled, professional and pleasant look with more variety; and could we add plugins from the composer too).
The plan's item 318 (the owner chose "Önce PR, sonra B grubu", 318 first): a "+" in place of the attach button with Add
files, Goal, Plan first, Save skill, then the plugins and the skills; a pick a chip with its mark and colour, one from the
slash menu the same chip; the run request takes `plugins` and `skills`, the run starts with those tool groups on and
the skill's text in its instructions. Until then the slash menu typed "use the skill NAME: " or a tool's name into the
box, and the model chose among every tool itself.

**As built (2026-10-16).** `store/models.py` `RunPicks` (`plugins`, `skills`, `plan_first`), `queued_messages.picks`
(an added column). `agent/picks.py`: `picks_problems` (a server that is not connected or none of whose tools the run
may use, its mode's within its agent's bounds; a skill not offered; Plan first in a chat or where nobody can be asked,
as under YOLO), `with_picks` (the first message: the owner's words, the servers to use, Plan first, each skill as
`tools/skill.py` `skill_instructions` renders it), the `picks` event. `agent/loop.py`: `RunOpening.picks`; a grouped run
starts with the picked servers' groups on; the goal message is `_opening_text`; `run.goal` stays the owner's words.
`agent/manager.py`: `start_picked` (`start` is it without picks), `start_for_agent` and `queue` take picks, and
`_check_picks` refuses at the launch and at the queue. `server/views.py`: `plugins` (8 at most), `skills` (4) and
`plan_first` on `StartRunRequest` and `QueueMessageRequest`, refused with `standing`. Save skill: `agent/playbooks.py`
`save_playbook` and `unsavable`, `POST /api/runs/{id}/skill`. Web UI: `picks.js` (the chips, their colours from the
characters' palette), `composer.js` (the "+" menu, the slash menu's picks, the draft keeps them), `choices.js` (goal
mode moves from Options to the "+", a chat hides it and Plan first), the home's, a run's and an agent's composer send
them, a steer keeps them and says so, `timeline.js`/`messages.js` (the chips under a sent message), `app.css`. README:
the web UI. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_composer_picks.py` (with the fixture MCP server and the scripted model: a picked
server's group on at step 0 and its tools in the first request, without the pick off; the skill and Plan first in the
first message and not in the goal; a queued message keeps its picks; six refusals over HTTP and nothing started; Save
skill writes a skill after one acting step and refuses a run with none; in the browser at 1280 px light and 390 px dark,
the "+" menu, the chips, the ×, the slash pick, the chips under the sent message, nothing wider than its box, no error in
the console), `test_composer.py` and `test_dock_choices.py` (goal mode in the "+"). Without the loop's change the
group test and the queue test fail (`on: ['core']`). Not tested: what a real model does with Plan first and a picked
skill.

**After the review (2026-10-16).** An independent review against the criteria found three things to fix first, and
they are fixed:

- A run on one of OpenCode's models goes whole to OpenCode's own agent (item 283), whose first message is the owner's
  words alone, so its picks were taken and then dropped without a word. `_check_picks` now refuses any pick on such a
  model, with why.
- Steering a queued message into the run at work (the row's button, or ⌘⇧Enter with an empty box) dropped its picks.

- That a run that goes on from another (resumed, or started by an answer after its run ended) starts without picks was

Also from the review: the Options tooltips no longer name goal mode, and the README gives the "+" menu's order as it
is (Add files, Save skill in a run's box, Goal mode, Plan first, Plugins, Skills). The tests add the OpenCode refusal

### 328. A phone that comes back to Dot finds it calm

**Status: done.** Merged as `34ad323` (PR #328; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** The owner's word of 2026-10-16, with five screenshots of another app on a phone: "Web tarafinda
mobilde hala istedigim sabiyeti ve netligi hisswdemiyorum. Uygulamayi arka plana atip baska seylere ugrasip tekrar
dondugumde daha sakin gelen bir UI istiyorum" (on the phone they still miss the steadiness and clarity they want; coming
back to the app from other things, they want it to come back calmer). Measured in WebKit as their iPhone 17 Pro Max,
with a proxy acting out a phone's network: back from the background on a network that woke in 4 s, a chat's page said
"Reconnecting" and put "Connection lost. Reconnecting…" into the conversation at about 2 s, which pushed it down 36 px
until about 4 s, and then drew the page again (about 118 elements added and 92 taken out, every row of the sidebar made
anew). Opened again after the page was let go, the page waited for the network for its own files, since the service
worker asked the network first, then showed Dot's card with "Connecting to the daemon…", a blank page, a spinner's card
for 3 s, and the chat at 5 s. The browser's bar was Dot's amber in both schemes, and the banner of a page that an
update left out of date sat in the bar and pushed the page down.

**As built (2026-10-16).**

- **Back from the background.** `state.js` `quietBreak`: for 8 s after the page comes back into view or onto the
  network (`RETURN_GRACE_MS`) a break of a stream says nothing; then the bar's pill shows, and on a chat's page a note
  that floats under the bar in a slot of no height (`.connection-slot`), so nothing read moves. `dom.js` `keepChildren`
  moves only the children that are out of place, and the sidebar keeps a chat's row while the chat and its family read
  the same, so a read after the return draws again only what changed.
- **Opened again.** `kept_pages.py` names the build of the pages in the `X-Dot-Pages` header of every file it serves,
  a 304 too, and writes it in `index.html`'s `dot-pages` meta. `sw.js` keeps its copies by build (`dot-pages-<build>`,
  one build at a time): a page whose network has not answered within 200 ms is answered from the copy, every file of it
  from the same copy, and such a page writes nothing to the copies. `state.js` compares the page's own build with the
  daemon's; at its start a page of another build loads again, once per build and tab, before it shows anything
  (`main.js`). `waiting.js`: while Dot waits for the daemon, a curtain shows the chat it opens on, its bar and its
  composer (the real `composerFrame`, with the draft) in the page's own classes. The run page keeps its title, the line
  under it and its placeholder for it (`keepChatLook`) and says when it shows its chat (`dot:page-ready`); the curtain
  lifts then, or after 3 s, and says that Dot connects only after 8 s. A wider window's curtain is the ground alone.
  The reads at the start go together.
- **The browser's bar.** `theme.js` `followBarColour` keeps one `theme-color` the colour of the page's ground as the
  theme, the scheme and the system's scheme change; `index.html` names the default theme's two grounds for the first
  paint.
- **Out of date.** The banner floats under the bar, and the page loads again once it is out of sight.
- **The row of Settings' tabs.** `views/settings.js` centres the open tab again once the fonts are in, unless the row
  was moved meanwhile. A page opened on Settings has the curtain's bare ground, with no words that ask for the webfont
  as "Connecting to the daemon…" did, so the font came in after the row was measured in the narrower fallback face,
  and the open tab ended 17 px past the row's edge (found by `test_phone_pages`). With the font held back 0.8 s, the
  file before this item left the open tab at 297–395 px in a row of 12–378 px, and this one puts it at 280–378 px.
- README: the web UI's update banner and service worker, and the phone.
- Tests: `tests/smoke/test_phone_return.py` (WebKit as the owner's iPhone, a proxy as its network). Back after 30 s
  away on a network that wakes in 4 s: nothing at three heights of the screen moves, nothing says that the page
  reconnects, the missed steps show within 2 s of the network, and the rows of the sidebar and of the helpers that did
  not change are the same nodes; with the network away for 15 s the pill shows from 8 s and not before. Opened again
  on a network that wakes in 4 s: at 500 ms the chat's title and composer stand where the page has them once it is
  there (the composer to the pixel, the title within one), nothing says that Dot connects, no script or style sheet is
  asked of the daemon (`/` and `/sw.js` are, against every file of the shell before), and the chat opens at its foot.
  The bar is the ground's colour, light and dark. An outdated page's banner moves nothing, and the page loads again
  once put away. `tests/unit/test_pages_build.py`: the build in the header, also of a 304, and in the meta.
  Changed: `test_reconnect` gives the pill 10 s after a stop soon after a return, for the 8 s of quiet;
  `test_pages_tell`'s pages run without the service worker, which once it controlled the page took the queue's read
  past the test's route (6/6 with it blocked; why the pages before this item did not was not found).
  `test_run_chrome` (two tests), `test_chat_choices` and `test_takeover` wait for the curtain to lift after a reload
  on a chat: while it is up it carries the chat's bar, composer and layout in the page's classes, and a bare class
  finds two. Found by holding the curtain its full 3 s over the 26 files that reload or open a second page: those four
  failed, and pass with the wait, held and not. `test_phone_return`'s proxy closes on waking also a connection it
  took while the network slept and that was still on its way to the daemon, which the page's timers make while it is
  put away: through it the stream came back at once (3 of 7 runs failed before, 5 of 5 passed after).
- Not verified on a device: the status bar of an app on the home screen with `theme-color`, and how often iOS lets the
  page go.

On the iPhone 17 Pro Max in the light scheme, on 16 of the 22 views fewer than one character in ten was 15 px or more
(Agents 0.3 %), 1,296 characters were under 13 px, and 333 controls were under 44 px each way, the radios drawn for a
screen reader alone left out (15 on General, where the plan's first count, which took 36 such radios in, said 51). The
switch was 34 by 20 px and only the switch itself turned it, a step's duration showed only under a hovering pointer,
and some hints named the config file's keys (`[agent] context_tokens in config.toml`, `[judge] provider = "typesafe"`,
`[server] reach`).

**As built (2026-10-17).**

- **A phone** is a touch screen (`pointer: coarse`) 720 px wide or less, or under 500 px high on its side; an iPad and a

  the looks, the labels of a list of facts (`.kv dt`), the line about a turn's latest step and the sidebar's lines of
  what a run does and how many it delegated read at a hint's size there. Code keeps the size chosen for it (13 px).

  and the context meter. The composer's round buttons keep their 36 px in a clear ring. The switch is iOS's, a 52 by 32
  px track in a 64 by 44 px box, and `dom.js` `switchRow` lets a tap anywhere on a setting's row, a pick of the

### 333. `dotx setup` leads to a working model, and the home says when none answers

**Status: done.** Merged as `34ad323` (PR #328; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** The README's quick start ended at `uv sync` and `dotx doctor`; nothing set Dot up. Every default
model is an Ollama cloud model, so a new person without an Ollama account got no answer, and a missing key showed only
in Settings. Xcode's Command Line Tools, which `dotx service install` builds Dot.app with, were not among the
requirements.

**As built (2026-10-17).**

- `dotx setup` (`cli_setup.py`):
  - **This Mac.** It checks the macOS version, ripgrep, Chrome and Xcode's Command Line Tools (`xcode-select -p`, which
    opens no dialog), in `dotx doctor`'s rows. A row that fails stops it before anything is written. The Command Line
    Tools are needed only when the service is installed.
  - **Provider.** It asks for one: Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenCode Go or OpenCode Zen's free models.
  - **Key.** The provider's API key goes to Dot's `.env` file with mode 0600, as `dotx auth set` stores it. A key that is
    set is kept. Dot reads the Keychain but never writes it.
  - **Model.** It offers the provider's models that can call tools, the configured main model first when it is one of
    them. The model becomes `[models] main`, `fast` and `review`, and `vision` when it sees images.
  - **Service.** It installs the service, as `dotx service install` does.
  - **Flags.** `--model provider:model` and `--key-stdin` answer without a terminal; `--no-service` leaves the service
    as it is. A model its provider does not list, or one that cannot call tools, is refused, with what to do (`ollama
    pull`, `dotx models`), and no model is written.

### 334. The repository opens with a short README, its details under docs/

**Status: done.** Merged as `34ad323` (PR #328; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**What was found.** The README had 2,900 lines in 26 sections, most of them details for someone who already runs Dot,
with no picture, no guide for contributors and no changelog. `pyproject.toml` named three of the five providers and
had no links or classifiers, and nothing said plainly that Dot runs on macOS alone.

**As built (2026-10-17).**

- **README** (about 120 lines). It says what Dot is, on macOS only, with two pictures (a finished task on a Mac and on a
  phone; a run of the scripted model on a throwaway home, as the README says). Then the requirements, five steps to
  install with `dotx setup`, the first steps, the phone through Tailscale, the safety in short, the documentation and
  the licences.
- **docs/.** Fourteen pages take the README's sections word for word: the command line, models, runs and tools,
  autonomy, safety and privacy, the daemon, the phone, browser and computer use, memory and schedules, agents and
  campaigns, apps, MCP servers, skills and plugins, configuration, development and the known limits. Only their headings
  and links changed. A script checked that every relative link of the Markdown files reaches a file and a heading (87
  links in 23 files), and that every line of the old README is in the new files; the four that are not changed on
  purpose (the providers of the first lines, the Quick start's heading and commands).
- **New files.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` covers setting up, the gate's commands, the rules of the tests, the code and pull
  requests. `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` follows the Contributor Covenant 2.1, with reports through GitHub's Report content.
  `CHANGELOG.md` sums up the first public version under Unreleased. There are issue templates for a bug and a feature
  (a security problem goes to SECURITY.md's private reporting) and a pull request template.
- **pyproject.toml.** It names the five providers, and has keywords, classifiers (macOS only, Python 3.13, Alpha) and
  the project's links. The package's metadata was built with them offline; the lock is unchanged.
- SECURITY.md, the gate's workflow and a comment of `opencode/server.py` point at the pages under docs/ that now hold
  what they named in the README.
- Left as they are, for the owner to decide: ROADMAP.md in the repository, the item numbers in comments and in the
  pages, and a release on PyPI.
